asks: My cousin wants me to help run a shop in a town three days from here. Should I go?
Can I ask your advice? I've been offered work far from the Leaf. Go, or stay?

answers.label: Go, see somewhere new
answers.reply: You think so? Part of me hoped you'd say that.

answers.label: Stay, your life is here
answers.reply: My friends, my street, my bath on Thursdays. You're right.

answers.label: Try it for one season
answers.reply: A season. Not forever. Why didn't I think of that?

asks: My cousin wrote again. The shop's struggling without me. Does that change your advice?
Another letter from my cousin. They really need me now. What would you do?

answers.label: Go and help
answers.reply: Family first. I suppose I knew that already.

answers.label: It's not your burden
answers.reply: Hm. Kind of you to say. It doesn't feel that simple, though.

answers.label: Send help, not yourself
answers.reply: Money and a good apprentice. Practical. My cousin would like that.

asks: I had a row with my oldest friend over nothing at all. How do I fix it?
My best friend and I aren't speaking. It started over a teapot. A teapot! What do I do?

answers.label: Apologise first
answers.reply: Even if it wasn't my fault? Yes. You're right. It rarely matters whose fault.

answers.label: Give it a few days
answers.reply: Let the steam out first. Sensible.

answers.label: Turn up with food
answers.reply: Ha! Nobody stays angry over a warm bun.

answers.label: Say what really hurt
answers.reply: The real reason, not the teapot. That's harder. And better.

asks: I tried what you said, and my friend's still cold with me. Do I keep trying?
It didn't work. My friend still crosses the street when they see me. What now?

answers.label: Keep trying
answers.reply: You're right. Years of friendship are worth a few more knocks.

answers.label: Give them space
answers.reply: Wait for them to come to me. It'll be hard.

answers.label: Ask someone they trust
answers.reply: A go-between. The old way. Might be just the thing.

asks: My master at the workshop keeps giving me the worst shifts. Should I say something?
I always get the late shift and the dirty jobs. Do I complain, or put up with it?

answers.label: Speak up, politely
answers.reply: Polite but firm. I'll practise in the mirror first.

answers.label: Work harder, they'll notice
answers.reply: Show them. Quietly. That's the patient way.

answers.label: Find a better place
answers.reply: Plenty of workshops in the Leaf. Maybe you're right.

asks: My shifts are better now, but things feel awkward at the workshop. Did I do something wrong?
Everything's fair at work now, but my master barely speaks to me. Should I worry?

answers.label: No, it was right
answers.reply: You think so? Then I'll stand by it.

answers.label: Bring them tea one morning
answers.reply: A peace offering. Small, but kind. Good idea.

answers.label: It'll pass
answers.reply: Awkwardness fades. Like a bruise. I'll wait it out.

asks: Am I too old to learn something new? I've always wanted to try pottery.
Everyone says pottery's for the young. Should I take it up anyway?

answers.label: Never too old
answers.reply: That's what I needed to hear. I'll ask at the potter's tomorrow.

answers.label: Start with something small
answers.reply: A cup. Then a bowl. Then a vase. A plan!

answers.label: Make me something first
answers.reply: Ha! My first student and my first customer. Deal.

asks: I made my first bowl. It's lopsided and it leaks. Should I keep going?
My pottery's dreadful. Truly. Do I give up?

answers.label: Keep going
answers.reply: Bowl number two, then. Thank you. I needed that.

answers.label: Use it for flowers
answers.reply: A leaky bowl for dry flowers. Ha! You see uses where I see failures.

answers.label: Take a proper lesson
answers.reply: Ask someone who knows. Swallow my pride. Fine.

asks: My little one wants to join the Academy. I'm scared to say yes. What would you do?
My child wants to be a ninja. Part of me is proud, part of me is terrified. Advice?

answers.label: Let them go
answers.reply: You're right. It's their dream, not my fear.

answers.label: Wait a year
answers.reply: A little older, a little steadier. Yes.

answers.label: Visit the Academy together
answers.reply: See it with my own eyes. Meet the instructors. Good.

asks: My child comes home from the Academy with a new bruise every day. Did I choose wrong?
Bruises, scrapes, and a sprained finger this week. Is this normal at the Academy?

answers.label: Bruises heal
answers.reply: Every ninja has a few, I suppose. You'd know.

answers.label: Talk to the instructor
answers.reply: Ask how they're doing. Properly. I will.

answers.label: Ask if they're happy
answers.reply: That's the real question, isn't it? Not the bruises.

asks: My neighbour's birthday is next week. What should I give?
I'm hopeless at gifts. What would you give a neighbour for their birthday?

answers.label: Something homemade
answers.reply: The time in it shows. I'll try my hand at a scarf.

answers.label: Food. Always food
answers.reply: A box of sweet buns. Nobody's ever been sad about sweet buns.

answers.label: Ask their friends
answers.reply: Spy a little. Find out what they really want. Clever.

answers.label: Flowers from the Yamanaka
answers.reply: The Yamanaka will know just the right bunch. Easy and lovely.

asks: A friend asked to borrow money. Last time they never paid it back. What do I do?
Lend again to someone who never paid you back before? I don't know what to say.

answers.label: Say no, kindly
answers.reply: An honest no. Hard but clean. You're right.

answers.label: Lend it again
answers.reply: Trust them again. You've a soft heart. So do I.

answers.label: Only what you can lose
answers.reply: If it comes back, a gift returned. If not, a gift. Wise.

asks: They paid me back, every ryo, and a bag of chestnuts on top! Was I wrong to doubt them?
My friend repaid the loan. With chestnuts! I feel terrible for doubting. Should I say so?

answers.label: Doubt was fair
answers.reply: After last time? I suppose it was. Still, I'm glad I was wrong.

answers.label: Tell them you doubted
answers.reply: Confess and clear the air. Brave. I'll do it over the chestnuts.

answers.label: Just be glad
answers.reply: You're right. Some things don't need saying. Just enjoying.

asks: My family's fished the river for five generations. I'm tired of it. Is that wrong?
Is it wrong to want a different trade from the one your family's always had?

answers.label: Not wrong. Change it
answers.reply: Five generations, ending with me. Hm. Or starting something new.

answers.label: Keep the family trade
answers.reply: You're right. It's who we are. I'll find the joy in it again.

answers.label: Do both for a while
answers.reply: Nets in the morning, something new in the afternoon. A gentle start.

asks: I told my family I want a different trade. They went quiet. What now?
Supper was silent last night. They know I want to change trades. How do I talk to them?

answers.label: Give them time
answers.reply: They'll come round. They always do, given a season.

answers.label: Show them a plan
answers.reply: Numbers and steps. Proof I'm serious. Yes.

answers.label: Go ahead anyway
answers.reply: My life, my trade. It's frightening. But you're right.

asks: I have to give a speech at my sister's wedding. I'm terrified. Any advice?
Speeches! Me! At a wedding! How do I get through it?

answers.label: Keep it short
answers.reply: Short and true. Nobody's ever complained a speech was too short.

answers.label: Tell a funny story
answers.reply: The time my sister fell in the river at eight. Perfect. She'll never forgive me.

answers.label: Practise on me
answers.reply: Really? You'd listen? Thank you. Sit down, this may take a while.

answers.label: Speak from the heart
answers.reply: Forget the notes. Just say how I feel. Terrifying. Right.

asks: The wedding speech went well! My cousin wants me to speak at theirs, too. Should I?
Everyone cried at my speech. Happy crying! Now I've been asked again. Do I say yes?

answers.label: Yes, you're good at it
answers.reply: Me, a speaker! Who'd have thought. All right.

answers.label: Only if you want to
answers.reply: Wise. I'll sleep on it.

answers.label: Let someone else shine
answers.reply: Hm, yes. My cousin's best friend would love the chance.

asks: I bet my friend I could out-eat an Akimichi. I lost. Badly. Do I have to pay up?
Never bet against an Akimichi at a barbecue. I did. Now I owe a week of chores. Pay up?

answers.label: Pay up
answers.reply: A bet's a bet. Fine. I'll be scrubbing pots till Sunday.

answers.label: Double or nothing
answers.reply: Ha! Against an Akimichi? You're crueller than you look.

answers.label: Laugh it off together
answers.reply: Buy them a drink and call it even. They'll probably agree.

asks: Confession: I nod along when people talk about chakra theory. I understand none of it. Do you ever pretend like that?
Have you ever nodded through a lesson without understanding a word?

answers.label: All the time
answers.reply: Ha! Thank goodness. I thought it was just me.

answers.label: Never, I ask questions
answers.reply: Brave. The question nobody asks is always the one everyone wanted to ask.

answers.label: Only in history class
answers.reply: Ha! The founding dates. Every single one of them.

asks: Is there something you've always been too embarrassed to ask? Ask me. I won't laugh.
Go on, ask me a question you'd never ask anyone else. I'll answer honestly.

answers.label: How taxes work
answers.reply: Ha! Nobody knows. Not even the tax office.

answers.label: Why people grow up
answers.reply: Oof. Ask me again when I've figured it out myself.

answers.label: What you think of me
answers.reply: Honestly? I think you're good company. There.

answers.label: I'll save it
answers.reply: Fair. The offer doesn't expire.

asks: I eat sweets before supper and tell everyone I don't. Got any secret habits?
Confession time: what's your guilty little habit?

answers.label: Snacks before bed
answers.reply: A shinobi after my own heart. Our secret.

answers.label: Talking to myself
answers.reply: Everyone does. The clever ones answer back.

answers.label: Skipping stretches
answers.reply: Don't let your sensei hear that. Your legs will tell on you.

answers.label: No habits at all
answers.reply: None? Hm. I'll catch you at one yet.

asks: When I was small I broke the shrine's bell rope and never told anyone. Ever broken something and kept quiet?
Have you ever broken something and hoped nobody would notice?

answers.label: Yes, and I owned up
answers.reply: Good for you. My bell rope still haunts me.

answers.label: Yes, and I hid it
answers.reply: Ha! We're the same, then. Our secrets are safe with each other.

answers.label: Never broken a thing
answers.reply: Never? Your hands must be made of silk.

asks: I've been thinking: should I finally tell the shrine keeper about that bell rope?
Thirty years later, is it too late to confess about the bell rope?

answers.label: Yes, tell them
answers.reply: You're right. It's been weighing on me long enough. I'll go tomorrow.

answers.label: Let it rest
answers.reply: You think so? It was a very old rope. Maybe that's mercy.

answers.label: Buy them a new rope
answers.reply: Ha! Confess with a gift in hand. You're a diplomat.

asks: I cried at the end of a puppet show last week. In public. Have you ever cried at a story?
Has a story ever made you cry? I won't tell a soul.

answers.label: Yes, more than once
answers.reply: A soft heart. Stories need people like you.

answers.label: Never
answers.reply: Never? We'll have to find you the right story.

answers.label: Only the sad dog ones
answers.reply: The dog ones! Always the dog ones. Every time.

asks: I get jealous of my brother sometimes. Everything comes easy to him. Do you ever feel that way about anyone?
Ever been jealous of someone, even a friend? It's all right to say.

answers.label: Yes, of a classmate
answers.reply: It's normal. Use it. Let it push you, not sour you.

answers.label: Not really
answers.reply: Lucky. Or very good at hiding it. Either way, good.

answers.label: Of people with families
answers.reply: Oh. I didn't think. Thank you for telling me. You're always welcome at our table.

asks: About that jealousy we talked about. Has it got easier?
Do you still feel it, that envy you told me about?

answers.label: Yes, much easier
answers.reply: Good. I'm glad. Mine's eased too, talking about it.

answers.label: It comes and goes
answers.reply: Like weather. I understand. Come and talk when it storms.

answers.label: It pushes me now
answers.reply: Then it's working for you instead of against you. Well done.

asks: I'm a grown adult and I'm frightened of the dark. Is there something small that scares you?
What's a silly little thing that frightens you? I'll tell you mine after.

answers.label: Thunder
answers.reply: Big booms. I'll admit I hide under a blanket too.

answers.label: Deep water
answers.reply: Wise to respect it. Stay near the shallows.

answers.label: Geese
answers.reply: Ha! Geese are terrifying. You're completely right.

answers.label: Nothing small
answers.reply: Only the big things? Hm. You're braver than me.

asks: If you could change one thing about yourself, would you?
Is there anything about yourself you wish were different?

answers.label: I'd be braver
answers.reply: You're braver than you think. I've seen it.

answers.label: I'd be stronger
answers.reply: Strength comes. Keep at it.

answers.label: I'd be more patient
answers.reply: Ha! Wouldn't we all.

answers.label: Nothing, I'm fine
answers.reply: Good. Liking yourself is half the battle won.

asks: That thing you wished was different about yourself. Do you still wish it?
Do you feel any closer to the person you want to be?

answers.label: Yes, I'm getting there
answers.reply: I can see it. You've changed since we talked.

answers.label: Not yet
answers.reply: "Yet" is a good word. Keep it.

answers.label: I've stopped wishing
answers.reply: You've made peace with it? That's a kind of strength too.

asks: I told my aunt I loved the scarf she knitted me. I hate it. I wear it anyway. Have you ever lied to be kind?
Have you ever told a fib just to make someone feel better?

answers.label: Yes, and I'd do it again
answers.reply: Me too. Some lies are a kind of gift.

answers.label: Yes, and I felt awful
answers.reply: It sits in the stomach, doesn't it? I know.

answers.label: I never lie
answers.reply: Never? Then I'll never ask you about my scarf.

asks: When did you last feel truly strong?
You told me what strength means. When did you last feel it yourself?

answers.label: Winning a spar
answers.reply: That rush when the other side yields. I remember it.

answers.label: Helping a friend
answers.reply: The quiet kind of strong. The best kind.

answers.label: Getting up after a fall
answers.reply: That's when it counts most. Nobody claps, but it counts.

answers.label: Not yet
answers.reply: It's coming. I'd bet on it.

asks: That fear you told me about. Have you ever faced it?
Have you ever looked your fear in the eye?

answers.label: Yes, and it shrank
answers.reply: Fears do that, once you face them. Most of them.

answers.label: Not yet
answers.reply: When you do, you won't be alone. Promise.

answers.label: A little, every day
answers.reply: Every day. That's the bravest answer there is.

asks: Is it harder to forgive other people, or yourself?
Forgiving others is one thing. Can you forgive yourself as easily?

answers.label: Myself, by far
answers.reply: Same for me. Be kinder to yourself. You'd be kind to anyone else.

answers.label: Other people
answers.reply: Then you're gentle with yourself. That's healthier than most.

answers.label: Both the same
answers.reply: Fair all round. That's rare.

asks: Would you ever lose on purpose, to make a friend happy?
A friend's having an awful week. You could let them win a spar. Would you?

answers.label: Never. They'd know
answers.reply: Fair. A thrown match is an insult to a good fighter.

answers.label: Yes, sometimes
answers.reply: A gift nobody sees. That's kind.

answers.label: Only at cards
answers.reply: Ha! Cards don't count. Everyone knows that.

asks: What's the biggest mistake you've made so far, if you can say?
Is there a mistake that still bothers you?

answers.label: Showing off
answers.reply: Showing off catches up with all of us. It's a good teacher.

answers.label: Not listening
answers.reply: To a teacher? To a friend? Either way, you're listening now.

answers.label: Being unkind once
answers.reply: It's good that it bothers you. It means you're not unkind.

answers.label: I'd rather not say
answers.reply: All right. It's yours to keep.

asks: The people you look up to. Have you ever told them?
Do they know you look up to them?

answers.label: Yes, I told them
answers.reply: Good. I'm sure it meant the world.

answers.label: Too embarrassed
answers.reply: Ha! It's never easy. Write it on a card.

answers.label: They know
answers.reply: Some things don't need words. Still, words are nice.

asks: What's your best memory of your favourite season?
Tell me one perfect day from your favourite time of year.

answers.label: A festival night
answers.reply: The lanterns, the music. Those nights stay with you.

answers.label: Training in it
answers.reply: Ha! Of course. Sweat or snow, you were out there.

answers.label: A quiet afternoon
answers.reply: The quiet ones are often the best.

answers.label: Haven't had it yet
answers.reply: Then let's make one. Next time the season comes round.

asks: What's the best gift you've ever given someone?
Not received, given. What gift are you proudest of?

answers.label: Something I made
answers.reply: Your own hands. That's a gift twice over.

answers.label: A meal I cooked
answers.reply: Feeding someone is the oldest kindness there is.

answers.label: An afternoon together
answers.reply: Time. You give what you value. That's nice to know.

answers.label: I haven't yet
answers.reply: Then that's something to look forward to.

asks: What do you think about, alone in that thinking spot of yours?
When you go off to think, what's usually on your mind?

answers.label: My dreams
answers.reply: Big ones, I hope. That's the place for them.

answers.label: My friends
answers.reply: Worrying about them, or missing them? Both, I'd guess.

answers.label: Nothing at all
answers.reply: Ah, the best kind of thinking. Empty and quiet.

answers.label: What comes next
answers.reply: Planning ahead. A shinobi's mind.

asks: If you were Lord Hokage for a day, what's the very first thing you'd do?
Say the hat's yours tomorrow morning. First order?

answers.label: Free ramen for all
answers.reply: Ha! You'd be the most popular Hokage in history.

answers.label: Visit every family
answers.reply: Every single door? That's a long day. And a lovely one.

answers.label: Train the Genin myself
answers.reply: Hands-on! The Genin would never forget it.

answers.label: Fix the roads
answers.reply: Practical! The carters would weep with joy.

asks: Why that nature, do you think? What draws you to it?
The nature you picked. What is it about it that fits you?

answers.label: It suits my temper
answers.reply: Ha! I can see it, now you say it.

answers.label: It's the most useful
answers.reply: Practical choice. A good shinobi's reasoning.

answers.label: It's beautiful
answers.reply: That's a lovely reason. Jutsu can be beautiful.

answers.label: I don't really know
answers.reply: Some things just call to you. That's enough.

asks: And who would you most want to remember you?
Of everyone, whose memory of you matters most?

answers.label: My friends
answers.reply: Then be good to them. You already are.

answers.label: The whole village
answers.reply: Big dreams. Your face on the Rock, perhaps.

answers.label: Students, one day
answers.reply: A teacher at heart. I can see it.

answers.label: Just one person
answers.reply: Just one. I won't ask who. That's a precious thing.

asks: What if the same classmate blamed you a second time?
Twice now someone's blamed you for their mess. What do you do?

answers.label: Tell the instructor
answers.reply: Twice is a pattern. The instructor should know. Sensible.

answers.label: Face them myself
answers.reply: Brave. Calmly, though. Calm is stronger.

answers.label: Forgive them again
answers.reply: A big heart. Don't let it become a doormat.

asks: Would you take a friend to your favourite place, or keep it to yourself?
Your favourite spot. Do you share it, or is it yours alone?

answers.label: Take a friend
answers.reply: A good place is better shared. I'd go.

answers.label: Keep it to myself
answers.reply: Fair. Everyone needs one place that's only theirs.

answers.label: Only my closest friend
answers.reply: Just one. I hope one day that's me.

asks: If a clan ever invited you to join them, would you?
Say one of the old families asked you to take their name. Would you?

answers.label: Yes, gladly
answers.reply: A family and a tradition at once. I can see why.

answers.label: I'd stay clanless
answers.reply: Your own name, your own path. I respect that.

answers.label: Depends which clan
answers.reply: Ha! The Akimichi, for the food? Wise.

asks: And how would you protect it, the thing that's most worth protecting?
You said what's worth protecting in the Leaf. How will you do it?

answers.label: Become strong
answers.reply: Strong enough to stand in front. The old way.

answers.label: Know everyone
answers.reply: Know them, and you'll know when something's wrong. Clever.

answers.label: Keep the peace
answers.reply: The hardest job. Peace needs keeping every day.

answers.label: Stand watch
answers.reply: A night on the walls, every so often. Quiet and important.

asks: You find a purse full of ryo by the river. What do you do?
Say there's a fat coin purse lying on the bridge, no one about. Then what?

answers.label: Take it to the police
answers.reply: The proper way. The Uchiha police keep a lost-and-found, you know.

answers.label: Find the owner myself
answers.reply: Asking around the market? That's a kind afternoon's work.

answers.label: Keep it if nobody asks
answers.reply: Hm. I'll keep a close eye on my own purse, then.

answers.label: Ramen for everyone
answers.reply: Ha! Generous with someone else's coin. I'll pretend I didn't hear.

asks: And if the purse belonged to someone who'd been rude to you?
Same purse, but the owner's the grump who shouted at you last week. Still give it back?

answers.label: Give it back anyway
answers.reply: Good. Their manners are their business. Yours are yours.

answers.label: Give it back with a look
answers.reply: Ha! A small, satisfied look. I'll allow it.

answers.label: Let someone else do it
answers.reply: Hm. It gets back either way, I suppose.

asks: Your friend is cheating at shogi against an old man in the park. Do you say something?
You catch a friend sneaking an extra piece onto the shogi board. Do you speak up?

answers.label: Call it out right there
answers.reply: Bold. They'll be embarrassed, but they'll remember.

answers.label: Have a word in private
answers.reply: Kind and honest. That's the hardest balance there is.

answers.label: Say nothing
answers.reply: Loyal to your friend. I'm not sure the old fellow would agree.

asks: Suppose you spoke up about the cheating, and your friend got angry with you. Then what?
What if telling the truth cost you a friend, at least for a while?

answers.label: Worth it
answers.reply: A friend worth having comes round. Truth holds.

answers.label: I'd say sorry
answers.reply: Sorry for the hurt, not for the truth, I hope.

answers.label: Let them cool off
answers.reply: A day or two of silence. Then dango. Then it's over.

asks: There's one dango left on the plate and two of you. What happens?
Last dango. You and a friend both reach for it. Who gets it?

answers.label: They can have it
answers.reply: That's a real friend. Or a full stomach.

answers.label: Split it in half
answers.reply: Fair's fair. Half a dango is still a dango.

answers.label: Race them for it
answers.reply: Ha! Ninja reflexes for dessert. I like it.

answers.label: Already ate it
answers.reply: Ha! Fast hands. Shameless, but fast.

asks: A friend tells you a secret, and it worries you. Do you keep it?
If keeping a friend's secret might let them get hurt, would you still keep it?

answers.label: Keep it
answers.reply: Loyal to the end. Just make sure the secret doesn't cost them.

answers.label: Tell an adult
answers.reply: The hard choice, and probably the right one.

answers.label: Talk to my friend first
answers.reply: Give them the chance to fix it themselves. Wise.

asks: Have you ever kept a secret that was really hard to keep?
Is there a secret you've carried a long time? You don't have to say what.

answers.label: Yes, and I kept it
answers.reply: Then you're someone people can trust. That's worth a lot.

answers.label: No one tells me secrets
answers.reply: Ha! They will. You've the face for it.

answers.label: I'd rather not say
answers.reply: That's an answer too. A careful one.

asks: You promised to meet a friend, but on the way a stranger needs help. What do you do?
Late for a friend, and someone's cart has lost a wheel in front of you. Stop or keep going?

answers.label: Help the stranger
answers.reply: Your friend will understand. A good friend always does.

answers.label: Keep my promise
answers.reply: Your word first. The stranger will find someone.

answers.label: Help fast, then run
answers.reply: Ha! The ninja answer: do both, quickly.

asks: A shopkeeper gives you too much change. Do you say anything?
The grocer counts your change wrong, in your favour. Do you point it out?

answers.label: Give it back
answers.reply: Good. The grocer will remember that, too.

answers.label: Keep quiet
answers.reply: Hm. Lucky for you I'm not the grocer.

answers.label: Spend it in the shop
answers.reply: Ha! It goes back to them either way. Sly.

asks: Your rival twists an ankle right before your match. Do you still fight?
Would you take a win against someone who's hurt?

answers.label: Wait till they're healed
answers.reply: A win means more when it's fair. Good.

answers.label: Fight, they'd want it
answers.reply: You know your rival. Maybe they'd be insulted otherwise.

answers.label: Ask them
answers.reply: Let them choose. That's respect.

asks: A classmate breaks something and blames you. What do you do?
Someone points at you for a mess they made. How do you handle it?

answers.label: Tell the truth
answers.reply: Straight out. Good. Nobody should carry someone else's broken pot.

answers.label: Take the blame
answers.reply: That's kind. Maybe too kind. Don't make a habit of it.

answers.label: Talk to them first
answers.reply: Give them the chance to own up. That's generous.

asks: Your squad wants a shortcut through dangerous woods to finish faster. Do you agree?
The long road is safe. The short one goes through bear country. Which do you take?

answers.label: The long road
answers.reply: Slow and sure. Your sensei will approve.

answers.label: The shortcut
answers.reply: Brave! Keep your eyes open and your kunai ready.

answers.label: Scout it first
answers.reply: Look before you leap. That's a good shinobi talking.

asks: Have you ever taken a risk you regretted?
The shortcut talk got me thinking. Ever jumped too fast and wished you hadn't?

answers.label: Yes, and I learned
answers.reply: Then it paid for itself. That's how I see mine.

answers.label: No, never
answers.reply: Never? Either you're very lucky or very careful.

answers.label: Regrets come later
answers.reply: Ha! Jump first, worry after. Bold.

asks: On a mission, you pass a farmer with a cart stuck in the mud. Stop to help, or keep going?
The mission has a deadline, but someone on the road needs a hand. What wins?

answers.label: Stay on the mission
answers.reply: The client's paying for your time. Fair enough.

answers.label: Stop and help
answers.reply: The Leaf's ninja helping on the road. That's how we got our good name.

answers.label: Help, but quickly
answers.reply: A quick shove and away. Practical.

asks: What's your favourite kind of weather?
If you could pick tomorrow's weather, what would it be?

answers.label: Bright sunshine
answers.reply: Warm stones and dry training grounds. Good choice.

answers.label: Soft rain
answers.reply: The village smells lovely after rain, doesn't it?

answers.label: Fresh snow
answers.reply: Snowball fights on the Academy field! Count me in.

answers.label: A big thunderstorm
answers.reply: Ha! Bold. I'll be indoors with my head under a blanket.

asks: Do you read for fun, or only scrolls for training?
What sort of stories do you like?

answers.label: Adventure tales
answers.reply: Roads, monsters and treasure. The scroll shop keeps a whole shelf.

answers.label: Training scrolls only
answers.reply: All work! I'll lend you a story. You'll thank me.

answers.label: Not much of a reader
answers.reply: That's all right. Some people read people instead.

answers.label: Poems, sometimes
answers.reply: Poems! I didn't expect that. I like you more for it.

asks: Do you sing, or play anything?
Music: are you a singer, a player, or a listener?

answers.label: I sing, badly
answers.reply: Badly is the best way to sing. Loudly, too, I hope.

answers.label: I'd like to learn flute
answers.reply: The old flute-maker by the shrine gives lessons. Just saying.

answers.label: I just listen
answers.reply: Listeners are what musicians need most.

answers.label: Festival drums
answers.reply: Ha! Of course. Loud and proud.

asks: After a long day, hot bath or a cold swim in the river?
Bathhouse or river? Which is the real cure for sore legs?

answers.label: Hot bath, always
answers.reply: The bathhouse at dusk. Nothing better.

answers.label: Cold river swim
answers.reply: Brr! You're tougher than me.

answers.label: One, then the other
answers.reply: Hot then cold. The old shinobi way. You know your stuff.

asks: Do you collect anything?
Everyone has a little collection somewhere. What's yours?

answers.label: Smooth stones
answers.reply: From the river? I'll keep an eye out for good ones.

answers.label: Shuriken
answers.reply: Ha! A practical collection. And sharp.

answers.label: Recipes
answers.reply: A recipe collector! You must share some.

answers.label: Nothing, yet
answers.reply: Then let me start you off. Here. A button from my coat.

asks: How do you take your ramen? This matters.
At Ichiraku, what's your order? Be precise.

answers.label: Miso
answers.reply: Rich and warming. The sensible choice.

answers.label: Pork, extra pork
answers.reply: Ha! A serious order. I respect it.

answers.label: Salt broth
answers.reply: Clean and simple. A purist.

answers.label: Whatever's special
answers.reply: Adventurous! The cook will like you.

asks: How many bowls of ramen can you manage in one sitting?
What's your record at Ichiraku? Bowls, I mean.

answers.label: Just one, properly
answers.reply: One bowl, savoured. Very civilised.

answers.label: Three, easily
answers.reply: Three! I'd need a nap after.

answers.label: I've never counted
answers.reply: Not counting is how you end up at seven. Ha!

asks: Do you believe in luck?
Lucky charms, lucky days: is there anything to it?

answers.label: Yes, I do
answers.reply: So do I. I've got a lucky coin. Don't laugh.

answers.label: You make your own luck
answers.reply: Hard work wearing a lucky hat. I like that.

answers.label: Only bad luck
answers.reply: Ha! A pessimist. At least you're never disappointed.

asks: Would you rather be rich, or well-loved?
A fortune in ryo, or a village full of friends. Pick one.

answers.label: Well-loved
answers.reply: Friends over gold. Good. Friends don't get stolen.

answers.label: Rich
answers.reply: Ha! Honest. With money you can buy everyone dinner.

answers.label: Earn both
answers.reply: Greedy! And ambitious. I like it.

asks: Someone pulls a mean prank on you. Do you get even?
A classmate fills your sandals with mud. Revenge, or let it go?

answers.label: Get even
answers.reply: Ha! Careful. Pranks have a way of growing.

answers.label: Let it go
answers.reply: The bigger person. Hard, though, with muddy sandals.

answers.label: A kind prank back
answers.reply: Fill theirs with flowers! You're a menace. A sweet one.

asks: And if they pranked you back again? Where does it end?
Prank, counter-prank, counter-counter-prank. How do you stop it?

answers.label: I end it with a truce
answers.reply: A truce! With dango, I hope.

answers.label: I win, that's how
answers.reply: Ha! The prank war of the century. Leave my shop out of it.

answers.label: It never ends
answers.reply: A lifelong prank war. Some of the best friendships start that way.

asks: Would you rather lead, or follow someone you trust?
Captain or squadmate: which suits you better?

answers.label: Lead
answers.reply: A leader! Mind you listen as much as you talk.

answers.label: Follow a good leader
answers.reply: Following well is a skill too. Nobody says so often enough.

answers.label: Walk side by side
answers.reply: No front, no back. A good squad's like that.

asks: If you weren't training to be a shinobi, what trade would you pick?
Imagine a life without kunai. What would you do instead?

answers.label: A cook
answers.reply: A good cook is loved by the whole street. Fine choice.

answers.label: A carpenter
answers.reply: Building things that last. The Kinoshita would take you on.

answers.label: A medic
answers.reply: Healing people. A noble thing, ninja or not.

answers.label: A merchant
answers.reply: Ha! A sharp eye and a quick tongue. You'd do well.

asks: That other trade you'd pick. Would you ever try it, on your days off?
Would you learn a bit of that trade, just for yourself?

answers.label: Yes, I'd love to
answers.reply: Then ask around. Most of the Leaf's crafters love a curious student.

answers.label: No time, sadly
answers.reply: Training eats every hour. One day, maybe.

answers.label: I already do, a little
answers.reply: Really? You'll have to show me.

asks: In a squad, what role suits you best?
On a mission, where do you want to be: front, back or in the middle?

answers.label: The front line
answers.reply: First in. Brave. Look after yourself out there.

answers.label: Support and healing
answers.reply: Every squad needs someone watching everyone else.

answers.label: The planner
answers.reply: The quiet one with the map. Squads live or die by that one.

answers.label: The scout
answers.reply: Quick and quiet, out ahead. Sounds like you.

asks: Has your squad found its shape yet? Who does what?
Do you and your squad work well together now?

answers.label: Like clockwork
answers.reply: Lucky. Some squads take years.

answers.label: Still working it out
answers.reply: That's normal. Give it a few missions.

answers.label: We argue a lot
answers.reply: Arguing squads often turn out the closest. Strange but true.

asks: Would you ever keep an animal companion of your own?
A ninja dog, a messenger hawk, a fat cat: would you want one?

answers.label: A ninja dog
answers.reply: Talk to the Inuzuka. They match people and puppies very carefully.

answers.label: A messenger hawk
answers.reply: Letters across the whole land. Very useful.

answers.label: A lazy old cat
answers.reply: Ha! Someone to nap with. Perfect.

answers.label: No room, sadly
answers.reply: An apartment's no place for a big dog. Maybe a fish?

asks: Two of your friends are fighting, and both want you on their side. What do you do?
Caught between two quarrelling friends. Whose side are you on?

answers.label: Stay out of it
answers.reply: Neutral ground. Safe, if lonely.

answers.label: Side with who's right
answers.reply: Fair, if you can tell. It's usually murkier than that.

answers.label: Bring them together
answers.reply: The peacemaker. Hardest job in any friendship.

asks: What if, whatever you did, both friends ended up cross with you?
Say both of your quarrelling friends blamed you. Then what?

answers.label: Wait it out
answers.reply: They'll miss you before they miss being angry.

answers.label: Apologise to both
answers.reply: Even if you did nothing wrong? Generous.

answers.label: Tell them the truth
answers.reply: "You're both being silly." Ha! Brave.

asks: A little child is lost at the market, crying, and you're due at training. What do you do?
Late for training, and there's a lost little one by the fish stalls. Stop, or keep going?

answers.label: Find their family
answers.reply: Of course you would. Training can wait for that.

answers.label: Fetch the police, then go
answers.reply: Hand them to someone who can help, then go. Sensible.

answers.label: Bring them to training
answers.reply: Ha! The youngest trainee in the Leaf. Your sensei's face!

asks: You borrowed a friend's kunai and lost it. Tell them, or quietly buy a new one?
Your friend's lucky kunai is at the bottom of the river, thanks to you. What now?

answers.label: Tell them
answers.reply: Honest. Hard. They'll trust you more for it.

answers.label: Replace it quietly
answers.reply: Spare them the worry. Kind, if they never notice.

answers.label: Tell them and replace it
answers.reply: Both. That's the full apology.

asks: Who makes the best food in the village?
Settle an argument for me: best cooking in the Leaf?

answers.label: Ichiraku
answers.reply: The classic answer, and probably the right one.

answers.label: The dango stand
answers.reply: Sweet and quick. The dango seller will be thrilled.

answers.label: Akimichi barbecue
answers.reply: Nobody grills like the Akimichi. Nobody.

answers.label: Whoever's feeding me
answers.reply: Ha! The most diplomatic answer in the village.

asks: If they carved one more face on the Hokage Rock, whose should it be?
The Rock has room for more faces. Who deserves the next one?

answers.label: The next Hokage
answers.reply: Fair. That's what the Rock is for.

answers.label: An ordinary villager
answers.reply: A baker, a teacher, a farmer. Now there's an idea.

answers.label: Mine, obviously
answers.reply: Ha! I'll bring a chisel and a ladder.

answers.label: A good dog
answers.reply: A dog on the Hokage Rock! The Inuzuka would never stop cheering.

asks: Do you think the village's rules for young ninja are too strict?
Curfews, training-ground hours, the forest out of bounds. Too much, or fair?

answers.label: They keep us safe
answers.reply: Sensible. Most rules have a scar behind them.

answers.label: Too strict
answers.reply: Ha! Every young ninja says that. Every old one said it too.

answers.label: Some are, some aren't
answers.reply: Fair and honest. Which ones, I wonder?

asks: If you could change one village rule, which would it be?
One rule, gone tomorrow. Which do you pick?

answers.label: Later curfew
answers.reply: An hour more of evening. The noodle shops would thank you.

answers.label: None, honestly
answers.reply: None? You're more patient than I ever was.

answers.label: Open the forest trails
answers.reply: The forest is lovely in spring. Mind the boars, though.

asks: What did you think of the Leaf, the first time you walked its streets?
Do you remember your first look at the village? What struck you?

answers.label: It was so big
answers.reply: The Hokage Rock, the rooftops going on forever. I remember that feeling too.

answers.label: Noisy and warm
answers.reply: Hawkers shouting, someone always cooking. That's the Leaf.

answers.label: Lonely, at first
answers.reply: At first. I hope "at first" is the important part.

answers.label: Like home already
answers.reply: Some places just know you. I'm glad this one did.

asks: Does the Leaf feel more like home now?
Now that you've been here a while, is this place home?

answers.label: Yes, it's home
answers.reply: Good. That makes me happier than I can say.

answers.label: Getting there
answers.reply: Getting there is fine. Homes take time to settle into.

answers.label: Not yet
answers.reply: That's honest. I'll keep the lantern lit till it does.

asks: What's the best day you've had in the Leaf so far?
If you could live one day here over again, which would it be?

answers.label: A festival day
answers.reply: Lanterns and music and everyone out. A good choice.

answers.label: A day with friends
answers.reply: Not what you did, but who with. Lovely.

answers.label: A training breakthrough
answers.reply: The day something finally clicked. I know that feeling.

answers.label: Maybe today
answers.reply: Today? Ha! Then I'll try not to spoil it.

asks: And the hardest day you've had here? You don't have to say.
There's always a bad day too. What was yours, if you'll tell me?

answers.label: A test I failed
answers.reply: One failed test. And you're still here, still trying. That's what matters.

answers.label: A day I felt alone
answers.reply: I'm sorry. Next time, come and find me. I mean it.

answers.label: A fight I lost
answers.reply: Losing hurts. It also teaches. You've grown since, I can tell.

answers.label: I'd rather not say
answers.reply: That's all right. The door's open if you ever want to.

asks: What do you remember most about your first weeks at the Academy?
Your first days at the Academy: what stuck with you?

answers.label: The instructor
answers.reply: A good teacher at the start makes all the difference.

answers.label: Making friends
answers.reply: The best thing the Academy gives you, if you ask me.

answers.label: Failing a test
answers.reply: Ha! Everyone fails one. The good ones fail early.

answers.label: The lunches
answers.reply: The rice balls by the window. Some things never change.

asks: Is there anyone from the Academy you're especially glad you met?
Of everyone in your class, who are you gladdest to know?

answers.label: A friend for life
answers.reply: Hold on to that one. Friends from the Academy stay.

answers.label: My rival, oddly
answers.reply: Ha! The ones who push us are a gift. An annoying gift.

answers.label: Everyone, really
answers.reply: A generous heart. Your whole class is lucky.

answers.label: Not yet
answers.reply: Classes are long. There's still time.

asks: What did you buy with the first ryo you ever earned?
First mission pay, first ryo of your own: where did it go?

answers.label: Ramen
answers.reply: Straight to Ichiraku. A proper start.

answers.label: Kunai
answers.reply: Tools before treats. A shinobi already.

answers.label: I saved it
answers.reply: Saved! I'm impressed. My first coin was gone in an hour.

answers.label: A gift for someone
answers.reply: Your first pay, and you spent it on someone else. That says a lot.

asks: How are you finding your apartment?
Is your apartment treating you well? Warm enough? Leaky roof?

answers.label: Cozy
answers.reply: Good. A cozy home is worth more than a big one.

answers.label: A bit too quiet
answers.reply: Quiet can be loud, can't it? Come visit whenever you like.

answers.label: Messy, honestly
answers.reply: Ha! Everyone's apartment is messy. Mine too. Don't look.

answers.label: I've decorated it
answers.reply: Really? You'll have to show me sometime.

asks: Do you ever get lonely in that apartment at night?
When it's late and quiet at home, how are you, really?

answers.label: Sometimes
answers.reply: Thank you for telling me. Sometimes is all right. You're not the only one.

answers.label: No, I like the quiet
answers.reply: Good. Quiet you choose is a fine thing.

answers.label: I visit friends instead
answers.reply: Smart. My door counts. Knock any evening.

answers.label: I'd rather not talk about it
answers.reply: All right. I won't push. Just know I asked because I care.

asks: When did you last laugh so hard it hurt?
What's the funniest thing that's happened to you here?

answers.label: With my friends
answers.reply: Nothing better than laughing till your sides ache with friends.

answers.label: A training mishap
answers.reply: Ha! Somebody fell off a training post, didn't they?

answers.label: I can't remember
answers.reply: Then we'll have to fix that. Soon.

answers.label: Just now
answers.reply: Ha! Was it my face? It's my face, isn't it?

asks: What's something you've done here that you're proud of?
Tell me one thing you've done that you're proud of. Don't be modest.

answers.label: Passing a hard test
answers.reply: Hard tests make the best memories. Afterwards.

answers.label: Helping someone
answers.reply: That's the best kind of pride there is.

answers.label: Not giving up
answers.reply: Stubbornness. The most underrated shinobi skill.

answers.label: Making a friend
answers.reply: A friend made is worth more than a test passed.

asks: Has anyone ever told you they were proud of you?
Does anyone tell you when you've done well?

answers.label: Yes, my teachers
answers.reply: Good. Teachers notice more than they say.

answers.label: Not really
answers.reply: Then I'll say it: I'm proud of you. There.

answers.label: My friends do
answers.reply: Friends who say it out loud. Keep those ones close.

asks: What's the most important thing you've learned since coming to the Leaf?
If you had to teach a newcomer one thing about life here, what would it be?

answers.label: Friends matter most
answers.reply: Took me years to learn that. You're ahead of me.

answers.label: Hard work pays off
answers.reply: It does. Slowly, and then all at once.

answers.label: Ask for help
answers.reply: The hardest lesson of all. I'm glad you've learned it.

answers.label: Never skip breakfast
answers.reply: Ha! The wisest thing anyone's told me this week.

asks: That lesson you told me about. Who taught it to you?
Where did you learn that, if you don't mind me asking?

answers.label: A teacher
answers.reply: Then that teacher did their job, and then some.

answers.label: A friend
answers.reply: The best lessons come from friends. They don't charge.

answers.label: I learned it alone
answers.reply: The hard way. Those lessons stick hardest.

answers.label: The village itself
answers.reply: Ha! The Leaf is a good teacher, isn't it? Strict, but fair.

asks: What kind of shinobi do you want to be?
Years from now, in a Jonin vest, what kind of ninja will you be?

answers.label: One who protects people
answers.reply: A shield, then. The village needs those more than swords.

answers.label: The strongest one
answers.reply: Big dream! Train hard enough and who knows.

answers.label: The cleverest one
answers.reply: Brains over brawn. The Nara would like you.

answers.label: One who sees the world
answers.reply: Out past every border. I hope you write.

asks: You told me what kind of shinobi you want to be. What made you want that?
Where did that dream come from, if you don't mind me asking?

answers.label: Someone I admire
answers.reply: Then they did something right. You should tell them one day.

answers.label: I want to prove myself
answers.reply: To who? No, don't answer. Just prove it to yourself first.

answers.label: I just know
answers.reply: Some people just know. That's rarer than you'd think.

answers.label: It's hard to explain
answers.reply: That's all right. The best reasons often are.

asks: Would you spend your whole life in the Leaf, or do you want to travel?
Stay here forever, or see what's past the hills?

answers.label: Stay in the Leaf
answers.reply: Roots are a good thing to have. This is a fine place to grow them.

answers.label: See the world
answers.reply: The roads go a long way. Don't forget the way back.

answers.label: Travel, then come home
answers.reply: The best of both. That's what I'd choose.

asks: If a mission would take you away for a whole year, would you go?
A year on the road, far from everyone here. Would you take it?

answers.label: Gladly
answers.reply: A year's nothing to a heart that wants to roam. Just come back.

answers.label: Only with my squad
answers.reply: Then home comes with you. Clever.

answers.label: I'd stay
answers.reply: Some people are needed where they are. No shame in that.

asks: Would you ever want to be Hokage?
Can you see your face up on the Hokage Rock one day?

answers.label: Yes, absolutely
answers.reply: Ha! Then I'd better be nice to you now.

answers.label: Too much paperwork
answers.reply: Ha! You've seen the stacks on that desk, haven't you?

answers.label: Maybe, one day
answers.reply: That's how every Hokage started, I bet.

answers.label: Someone better should
answers.reply: Modest. The best ones usually are.

asks: Are you in a hurry to make Chunin?
Some Genin rush the exams, some wait years. Which are you?

answers.label: As soon as I can
answers.reply: Fast and fearless. Just don't skip the lessons on the way.

answers.label: When I'm ready
answers.reply: The vest will wait. Better to earn it than grab it.

answers.label: Rank doesn't matter
answers.reply: A rare thing to hear from a shinobi. I like it.

asks: Where do you think you'll be in ten years?
Picture yourself ten years from now. What are you doing?

answers.label: Leading a squad
answers.reply: Captain. I can see it. Be the kind you'd want to follow.

answers.label: Running a shop
answers.reply: A ninja shopkeeper! Mind you keep the prices fair.

answers.label: Out on the road
answers.reply: Somewhere far off, with stories to send home.

answers.label: Here, with my friends
answers.reply: Then I'll save you a seat for ten years.

asks: If you could pick any chakra nature, which would you choose?
Fire, water, wind, earth, lightning. Which one feels like you?

answers.label: Fire
answers.reply: Bright and bold. The Sarutobi would cheer.

answers.label: Water
answers.reply: Calm on top, strong underneath. A good nature.

answers.label: Wind
answers.reply: Quick and sharp. You'd never stand still.

answers.label: Earth or lightning
answers.reply: Can't decide? Steady ground or a flash in the dark. Both good.

asks: What would your dream home be like?
If you could build any house you liked, what would it be?

answers.label: A big house, full of people
answers.reply: A table that seats twenty and a door that's never locked. Lovely.

answers.label: Quiet, by the river
answers.reply: Water outside the window, nobody knocking. Peaceful.

answers.label: Anywhere with a kitchen
answers.reply: Ha! Priorities. I respect that.

answers.label: A tent, always moving
answers.reply: A home on your back. Very free. Very damp, I'd guess.

asks: What would you want people to remember you for?
Long after, when people talk about you, what should they say?

answers.label: Being kind
answers.reply: That's the best thing anyone can be remembered for.

answers.label: Being strong
answers.reply: Strong for others, I hope. Then they'll remember it fondly.

answers.label: Keeping my word
answers.reply: "They always kept their word." A fine thing to have carved on a stone.

answers.label: Making them laugh
answers.reply: The village always needs one of those. Don't stop.

asks: If you could learn any jutsu tomorrow, what kind would it be?
Dream jutsu: what does it do?

answers.label: Something flashy
answers.reply: Fireworks from your hands! Very showy.

answers.label: Something that heals
answers.reply: A medic's touch. The hospital always needs more of those.

answers.label: Something sneaky
answers.reply: Invisible, silent, gone. Mind you don't use it to skip chores.

answers.label: Something that protects
answers.reply: A wall between your friends and trouble. I like that.

asks: What's your favourite food? I'm always looking for an excuse to eat.
If you could eat one thing every day, what would it be?

answers.label: Ramen, obviously
answers.reply: Ichiraku, I'd guess. Half the village would say the same.

answers.label: Dango
answers.reply: Three on a stick, sweet sauce. Good taste.

answers.label: Grilled fish
answers.reply: Salted, straight off the fire by the river. Simple and perfect.

answers.label: Whatever's free
answers.reply: Ha! A shinobi's answer if ever I heard one.

asks: If you cooked one meal for all your friends, what would you make?
Say you're hosting supper for everyone you know. What's on the table?

answers.label: A big hot pot to share
answers.reply: Everyone reaching into one pot. That's how a meal should be.

answers.label: Something I invented
answers.reply: Brave! I'll bring a backup rice ball, just in case.

answers.label: Takeout from Ichiraku
answers.reply: Wise. Nobody gets food poisoning that way.

asks: Which season do you like best?
Spring, summer, autumn or winter: which one's yours?

answers.label: Spring, for the blossoms
answers.reply: The cherry trees along the river. Nothing like them.

answers.label: Summer, for the festivals
answers.reply: Lanterns, fireworks, and too much shaved ice. Good choice.

answers.label: Autumn, for the leaves
answers.reply: The whole forest goes red and gold. I'd pick it too.

answers.label: Winter, for the snow
answers.reply: Brr. You must like hot baths afterwards.

asks: How do you like to train?
When you practise, what does a good session look like?

answers.label: Alone at dawn
answers.reply: Quiet field, cold air, no one watching. I know the feeling.

answers.label: Sparring with friends
answers.reply: More fun, and you learn more when someone hits back.

answers.label: Reading the scrolls
answers.reply: A thinker. The best fighters know why a move works.

answers.label: Until I drop
answers.reply: Careful with that. Rest is training too.

asks: What's the hardest thing your training has ever asked of you?
What part of being a shinobi is hardest for you, honestly?

answers.label: Being patient
answers.reply: Patience is a jutsu nobody can teach. You just have to live through it.

answers.label: Losing to someone
answers.reply: Losing teaches more than winning. It just doesn't feel like it.

answers.label: Trusting others
answers.reply: That's a deep one. I hope it gets easier.

answers.label: Getting up early
answers.reply: Ha! The great enemy of every Genin.

asks: Are you a morning person or a night owl?
Up with the sun, or up with the moon?

answers.label: Morning, always
answers.reply: The best hour of the day is the first one. Agreed.

answers.label: Night, definitely
answers.reply: The village is so quiet at night. It's like a different place.

answers.label: Neither, I like naps
answers.reply: Ha! A noon person. Rare, and wise.

asks: What do you do on a rainy day?
The rain's coming down hard. Where do you go?

answers.label: Train anyway
answers.reply: Rain makes the ground slippery. Good practice, I suppose.

answers.label: Read indoors
answers.reply: A scroll and a cup of tea by the window. Perfect.

answers.label: Jump in puddles
answers.reply: Ha! I hope you've got a dry pair of sandals at home.

answers.label: Sleep through it
answers.reply: Rain on the roof is the best sleeping sound there is.

asks: Where do you go when you need to think?
Everyone has a spot for thinking things through. Where's yours?

answers.label: The Hokage Rock
answers.reply: The whole village laid out below you. It makes problems feel smaller.

answers.label: The river
answers.reply: Water helps. It keeps moving, so your thoughts do too.

answers.label: The training grounds
answers.reply: You think with your fists? Ha. Sometimes it works.

answers.label: A rooftop at night
answers.reply: Up with the stars. I won't tell anyone where.

asks: What's the best gift anyone could give you?
If someone wanted to make your day, what should they bring?

answers.label: Something handmade
answers.reply: The time in it is the gift. I agree completely.

answers.label: Their time
answers.reply: Just being there. That's the rarest gift of all.

answers.label: A good meal
answers.reply: Practical and delicious. I like how you think.

answers.label: A new scroll
answers.reply: Something to learn. Of course you'd say that.

asks: Cats or dogs?
Important question: are you a cat person or a dog person?

answers.label: Dogs
answers.reply: Loyal, loud, and always happy to see you. The Inuzuka would approve.

answers.label: Cats
answers.reply: Independent. They love you on their own terms. Good choice.

answers.label: Birds
answers.reply: Birds! Now there's an answer I didn't expect.

answers.label: Any animal at all
answers.reply: You'd feed every stray in the village, wouldn't you?

asks: What's the best part of a festival, for you?
Festival night. Where am I most likely to find you?

answers.label: The food stalls
answers.reply: Squid on a stick, candied apples, sweet corn. Lead the way.

answers.label: The fireworks
answers.reply: Lying on the grass, watching the sky burst. Lovely.

answers.label: The games
answers.reply: The goldfish scoop! Everyone's terrible at it.

answers.label: Being with friends
answers.reply: The festival's just the excuse, isn't it?

asks: You get a whole day free: no training, no missions. What do you do?
A day off with nothing planned. How do you spend it?

answers.label: Explore past the gate
answers.reply: Out into the forest? Take a map. And a snack.

answers.label: Wander the village
answers.reply: There's always a new shop or a lane you've never walked.

answers.label: Sleep till noon
answers.reply: The most honest answer anyone's ever given me.

answers.label: Spend it with friends
answers.reply: Doesn't matter where, then. Just who.

asks: Sweet or salty?
Red bean bun or salted rice cracker?

answers.label: Sweet
answers.reply: Red bean paste, then. A sweet tooth is a happy tooth.

answers.label: Salty
answers.reply: Crackers and pickles! Someone after my own heart.

answers.label: Both at once
answers.reply: Sweet soy dango. The best of both. You're clever.

asks: Say a friend proudly shows you a painting, and it's dreadful. What do you tell them?
A friend made you a scarf. It's lumpy and the colours fight. Do you say so?

answers.label: The truth, gently
answers.reply: Gently is the hard part. Good for you.

answers.label: That I love it
answers.reply: Sweet of you. I hope they never find out.

answers.label: Ask what they like about it
answers.reply: Clever. Let them find the flaws themselves.

answers.label: Ask for lessons
answers.reply: Ha! Then you'd both be painting dreadfully. Together, at least.

asks: Has anyone ever told you something true that you didn't want to hear?
Was there ever a hard truth you were glad someone said to you?

answers.label: Yes, and I'm grateful
answers.reply: That takes a good friend on both sides.

answers.label: Yes, and it still stings
answers.reply: Some truths take a long time to settle. That's all right.

answers.label: I'd rather not have known
answers.reply: Maybe. Some things are kinder left unsaid.

asks: If breaking a rule would get the mission done, would you break it?
Rules or results? If you can only have one, which do you pick?

answers.label: Rules come first
answers.reply: The rules are there because someone learned the hard way.

answers.label: The mission comes first
answers.reply: Results. Bold. Just make sure you can explain it afterwards.

answers.label: Depends on the rule
answers.reply: Fair. Some rules are walls, and some are fences.

asks: Your sensei orders you to leave a hurt teammate and finish the mission. What do you do?
Orders say go on. Your teammate is down behind you. Which way do you run?

answers.label: Follow the order
answers.reply: That's a heavy thing to carry. I hope you never have to.

answers.label: Go back for them
answers.reply: I'd want you on my squad. Even if the sensei shouted.

answers.label: Find a third way
answers.reply: There usually is one, if you're quick enough to see it.

asks: What does being strong mean to you?
When you say someone's strong, what do you mean?

answers.label: Winning fights
answers.reply: Simple and honest. There's something to be said for that.

answers.label: Protecting people
answers.reply: That's the kind of strong that lasts.

answers.label: Never giving up
answers.reply: Getting up one more time than you fall. I like that.

answers.label: Knowing yourself
answers.reply: That's a quiet answer. Quiet answers are usually the deep ones.

asks: Do you work better on your own, or with others around?
Alone or in a team: where do you do your best work?

answers.label: On my own
answers.reply: No one to slow you down. No one to catch you, either.

answers.label: With a team
answers.reply: More hands, more ideas, more lunch.

answers.label: Depends on the team
answers.reply: Ha! Yes. The right team, or no team at all.

asks: When something's really wrong, do you tell someone, or handle it yourself?
Is it hard for you to ask for help?

answers.label: I handle it myself
answers.reply: I understand. Just remember the door's open.

answers.label: I tell a friend
answers.reply: Good. That's not weakness. It's sense.

answers.label: I'm learning to ask
answers.reply: That's honest. It's harder than any jutsu, I think.

asks: Can I ask you something? What frightens you most?
Everyone's afraid of something. What's yours?

answers.label: Being alone
answers.reply: That one I understand. You're not, you know. Not here.

answers.label: Letting people down
answers.reply: Then you care a great deal. That's not a bad fear to have.

answers.label: Spiders. Big ones
answers.reply: Ha! A sensible fear. Some of them are the size of my hand.

answers.label: Nothing at all
answers.reply: Nothing? Hm. Ask me again in a few years.

asks: Is it ever all right to break a promise?
Could you break your word, if keeping it would hurt someone?

answers.label: Never
answers.reply: Your word is all you really own. I respect that.

answers.label: To spare someone pain
answers.reply: Kindness over your word. I can see that.

answers.label: Only if I explain why
answers.reply: That's the honest way to break one, I suppose.

asks: Someone wrongs you and then says sorry. Do you forgive them?
How long does it take you to forgive someone?

answers.label: Right away
answers.reply: You've a generous heart. Don't let anyone use it.

answers.label: Once they prove it
answers.reply: Sorry is a word. What comes after is the real apology.

answers.label: Depends what they did
answers.reply: Some things take a day. Some take years. True enough.

asks: Should we keep old customs, even when nobody remembers why?
The village has customs older than anyone alive. Keep them all, or let some go?

answers.label: Keep them
answers.reply: There's a reason somewhere, even if it's just to remember.

answers.label: Let the old ones go
answers.reply: A village has to breathe. I can't say I disagree.

answers.label: Find out why first
answers.reply: Ask an elder over tea. Usually there's a good story in it.

asks: If the elders decided something you thought was wrong, would you say so?
Would you stand up to the village council, if you were sure they were mistaken?

answers.label: I'd speak up
answers.reply: Brave. Do it politely, and they might even listen.

answers.label: I'd trust them
answers.reply: They've seen a lot. Still, keep your eyes open.

answers.label: I'd talk to them alone
answers.reply: Wise. No one likes being corrected in public.

asks: Does it matter how you win, or only that you win?
A win's a win, or is there such a thing as winning wrong?

answers.label: How you win matters
answers.reply: Then you'll never have to look away from anyone. Good.

answers.label: A win is a win
answers.reply: Ha! The scoreboard agrees with you.

answers.label: Depends who I'm fighting
answers.reply: Against a bandit, anything goes. Against a friend, play fair. Sensible.

asks: Who do you count as family?
Family isn't only blood, I think. Who's yours?

answers.label: My friends here
answers.reply: Then you've a big family. And I hope I'm in it.

answers.label: My squad
answers.reply: Squads become family. It's the oldest story in the Leaf.

answers.label: The whole village
answers.reply: The whole Leaf? That's a lot of birthdays to remember.

answers.label: I'm still finding out
answers.reply: That's all right. Families take time to find.

asks: What do you do after you make a big mistake?
When you've really messed something up, what happens next?

answers.label: Own up at once
answers.reply: Straight to it. That's harder than it sounds.

answers.label: Fix it quietly
answers.reply: Mend it and move on. Sensible, if no one's hurt.

answers.label: Learn from it
answers.reply: Then it wasn't wasted. That's how I see it too.

answers.label: Sulk for a day
answers.reply: Ha! Honest. A day of sulking, then back to work.

asks: Are little lies all right, if they keep the peace?
"That hat looks lovely on you." Little lies like that: harmless, or not?

answers.label: They're harmless
answers.reply: A bit of grease for the wheels. Most people agree.

answers.label: I'd rather not lie
answers.reply: Even about the hat? You're a stern one.

answers.label: Just don't comment
answers.reply: Ha! The silent compliment. Very diplomatic.

asks: Who do you look up to?
Is there someone you want to be like, one day?

answers.label: My teachers
answers.reply: Good teachers are worth looking up to. Tell them, sometime.

answers.label: My friends
answers.reply: You look up to your friends? That's a lovely thing to say.

answers.label: The Hokage
answers.reply: Aim high. That's the spirit of the Leaf.

answers.label: Nobody yet
answers.reply: Then you'll have to become someone worth looking up to.

asks: What's your favourite place in the village?
If I wanted to find you on a free afternoon, where would I look?

answers.label: Ichiraku
answers.reply: The counter, the steam, the smell of broth. Can't argue.

answers.label: The Hokage Rock
answers.reply: Up top, looking down at it all. Good view for thinking.

answers.label: The training grounds
answers.reply: Even on your day off? Dedicated.

answers.label: The river
answers.reply: The river by the second bridge. Quiet, and the fish are fat.

asks: If you could change one thing about the Leaf, what would it be?
Say you were Hokage for a day. What's the first thing you'd change?

answers.label: Nothing at all
answers.reply: Content with the Leaf as it is. That's rare. And nice to hear.

answers.label: More festivals
answers.reply: Ha! A festival every week. The dango sellers would crown you.

answers.label: Fewer rules
answers.reply: A freer village. The council would faint, but I see the appeal.

answers.label: More help for the lonely
answers.reply: That's a kind wish. More people need it than you'd think.

asks: Do you think the Leaf changes too fast, or not fast enough?
New shops, new streets, new faces every season. Too much, or too little?

answers.label: Too fast
answers.reply: I miss things already, and I'm not that old. I understand.

answers.label: Not fast enough
answers.reply: Impatient! The village will catch up with you one day.

answers.label: About right
answers.reply: Steady as a river. A good pace for a village.

asks: Do you think the clans make the village stronger?
Some families have been here since the Leaf was founded. Is that good for the village?

answers.label: Yes, they keep traditions
answers.reply: Old roots hold the soil. That's the usual argument, and a fair one.

answers.label: Everyone should be equal
answers.reply: Clan or no clan, the same headband. I like that.

answers.label: If they share what they know
answers.reply: Strength kept to yourself helps no one. Wise.

asks: Market Day: love it or hate it?
Do you like Market Day, with all the crowds and noise?

answers.label: Love the bustle
answers.reply: Everyone out, everyone shouting prices. It's the village's heartbeat.

answers.label: Too noisy
answers.reply: I'll find you hiding behind the library, then.

answers.label: Only for the snacks
answers.reply: Ha! The grilled corn alone is worth the crowds.

asks: What's most worth protecting in the Leaf, do you think?
If the Leaf could only keep one thing safe, what should it be?

answers.label: The people
answers.reply: Not the walls or the Rock. The people. That's right.

answers.label: The children
answers.reply: The next generation. That's what every Hokage has said.

answers.label: The old ways
answers.reply: The customs that make us the Leaf. A thoughtful answer.

answers.label: My friends
answers.reply: Start close and it spreads outward. Good.

asks: Would you rather live right by the market, or out at the quiet edge of the forest?
Busy street or quiet trees: where would you want your front door?

answers.label: By the market
answers.reply: Noise and neighbours and fresh bread every morning. Lovely.

answers.label: At the forest edge
answers.reply: Birds instead of hawkers. Peaceful.

answers.label: Somewhere in between
answers.reply: The residential lanes, then. Close enough to visit, far enough to sleep.

asks: Should the Leaf welcome more travellers from other lands?
More merchants and visitors from far away: good for the village, or not?

answers.label: Open the gates wide
answers.reply: New faces, new food, new stories. I'm for it.

answers.label: Carefully
answers.reply: Welcome, but with an eye on them. The gate guards would agree.

answers.label: Friends, not strangers
answers.reply: Get to know them first. A sensible middle.

asks: At the Leaf Festival, would you rather run a stall, or just enjoy it?
If you had a festival stall, what would you sell? Or would you rather just wander?

answers.label: Run a stall
answers.reply: Ha! I'd buy whatever you're selling. Probably.

answers.label: Just enjoy it
answers.reply: Fair. Someone has to eat all the food.

answers.label: Help a friend's stall
answers.reply: Always the helper. Every stall needs one.

asks: Have you ever walked the village late at night, when everyone's asleep?
Do you like the Leaf at night, with the lanterns out?

answers.label: Yes, it's peaceful
answers.reply: Just you and the night patrol. I know what you mean.

answers.label: Too spooky for me
answers.reply: Ha! The old shrine creaks, I'll admit.

answers.label: Only on the way home
answers.reply: Sensible. Bed is the best place at night.

asks: If I left tomorrow to walk to the sea, would you come?
I've got a map, two weeks of rice and a road to the coast. Coming?

answers.label: Yes, let's go
answers.reply: Ha! I knew it. Pack light and bring good sandals.

answers.label: I've got duties here
answers.reply: Right. Someone has to keep the village standing while I'm away.

answers.label: Bring me back a shell
answers.reply: Deal. The prettiest one on the beach.

asks: On a long road out of the Leaf, what would you most want to see?
Of everything out past the hills, what's calling you?

answers.label: The sea
answers.reply: Water to the edge of the sky. You never forget the first sight of it.

answers.label: The mountains
answers.reply: Snow on the peaks in summer. I've seen it once. I'll see it again.

answers.label: Other villages
answers.reply: Their food, their festivals, their way of doing things. You'd learn so much.

answers.label: The road itself
answers.reply: Ha! A true traveller. The going is the point.

asks: Have you ever slept under the stars, no roof at all?
Ever spent a night out in the open? Just you, a blanket and the sky?

answers.label: Yes, I loved it
answers.reply: Isn't it the best? You wake up with the birds.

answers.label: Not yet
answers.reply: Not yet! We'll fix that. Next clear night.

answers.label: Too many bugs
answers.reply: Ha! A small price for the stars. Bring a net.

asks: Better a safe life, or an exciting one?
If you had to pick: a quiet, safe life, or a wild one?

answers.label: Safe
answers.reply: Safe. Hm. I respect it, even if my feet itch just hearing it.

answers.label: Exciting
answers.reply: Ha! Now we're talking. Life's too short for safe.

answers.label: Exciting, then safe
answers.reply: Wild while you're young, a porch chair later. Good plan.

asks: Where's the line, though? How much danger is too much?
Even I turn back sometimes. When would you?

answers.label: When others could get hurt
answers.reply: Yes. Your own neck is yours to risk. Not theirs.

answers.label: There's no line
answers.reply: Ha! Careful. Even I have a line. It's just very far out.

answers.label: When I'm truly scared
answers.reply: Fear's a good guide, if you listen to it. Wise.

asks: If I gave you a map with a big blank space in the middle, what would you do?
A map with nothing drawn in one corner. What's your first thought?

answers.label: Go and fill it in
answers.reply: Ha! That's what I'd do. Bring a brush and ink.

answers.label: Ask why it's blank
answers.reply: Clever. Sometimes blank means "don't go". Sometimes it means "nobody dared".

answers.label: Draw a dragon there
answers.reply: Ha! The old mapmakers did exactly that. You'd fit right in.

asks: Past the border, where's the first place you'd go?
First trip far from home, where do you head?

answers.label: The sea
answers.reply: Salt air and fish fresh off the boat. You'll love it.

answers.label: A big city
answers.reply: Lanterns on every street and markets that never close. Exciting.

answers.label: The mountains
answers.reply: The cold up there clears your head like nothing else.

answers.label: Wherever the road goes
answers.reply: Ha! The best plan is no plan.

asks: Is it brave to go somewhere you know nothing about, or just foolish?
Walking into the unknown: courage or foolishness?

answers.label: Brave
answers.reply: That's my answer too. Someone has to go first.

answers.label: Foolish without a plan
answers.reply: Fair. A little planning makes a brave trip a living one.

answers.label: A bit of both
answers.reply: Ha! Honest. Most of my best trips were both.

asks: What's the furthest you've ever been from the Leaf?
How far past the gate have you been, so far?

answers.label: Just past the gate
answers.reply: A start! Every road starts a step past the gate.

answers.label: On a mission
answers.reply: A mission! Then you've tasted it. The road gets into you.

answers.label: Nowhere yet
answers.reply: Nowhere yet. Ooh, I'm jealous. The first time is the best.

asks: Out there, beyond the village, how did it feel?
When you looked back and couldn't see the Hokage Rock any more, what did you feel?

answers.label: Free
answers.reply: Free. Yes. That's exactly the word.

answers.label: A little scared
answers.reply: Everyone is, the first time. Means you're paying attention.

answers.label: I missed home
answers.reply: Missing home is how you know where home is.

answers.label: I haven't been out yet
answers.reply: Then it's still waiting for you. Lucky.

asks: If you could find out how one thing works, what would it be?
What's something you've always wanted to take apart and understand?

answers.label: How jutsu work
answers.reply: Chakra and hand signs! I've wondered that for years.

answers.label: How the stars move
answers.reply: Big question! The scroll keepers have charts, you know.

answers.label: How people think
answers.reply: The hardest puzzle of all. Let me know what you find.

answers.label: How ramen broth is made
answers.reply: Ha! That secret is better guarded than the Hokage's office.

asks: That thing you wanted to understand. Found anything out yet?
Any progress? On the puzzle you told me about?

answers.label: A little
answers.reply: A little! Tell me everything. Slowly. With diagrams.

answers.label: No, still wondering
answers.reply: Still wondering is the best part. Enjoy it.

answers.label: It's more complicated
answers.reply: Isn't it always? That's how you know you're getting close.

asks: Do you believe rumours?
When you hear gossip at the well, do you trust it?

answers.label: Never
answers.reply: Never? Not even the one about the dango seller's twin? Hm. Wise.

answers.label: Some of them
answers.reply: The trick is knowing which. I'm still working on it.

answers.label: Only the fun ones
answers.reply: Ha! Me too. Truth's overrated at the well.

asks: If you could ask Lord Hokage one question, what would it be?
One question, straight to Lord Hokage. What do you ask?

answers.label: How do you do it all
answers.reply: The paperwork alone! I'd love to know too.

answers.label: What's your favourite food
answers.reply: Ha! The important questions. I've always wondered.

answers.label: Can I see the office
answers.reply: The view from up there must be something. Bold!

answers.label: Who taught you
answers.reply: Oh, that's a good one. Every Hokage had a teacher.

asks: What did you learn today? Anything at all counts.
Tell me one thing you didn't know this morning.

answers.label: A new move
answers.reply: A new move! Show me. No, don't, not near the pots.

answers.label: Something about a friend
answers.reply: Ooh. Those are the best things to learn.

answers.label: Nothing yet
answers.reply: The day's not over! Let's find you something.

answers.label: A new word
answers.reply: Which word? Tell me. I collect them.

asks: What's the most surprising thing you've found out this week?
This week, what made you go "huh, really?"

answers.label: Something about the village
answers.reply: The village never runs out of surprises. Tell me!

answers.label: Something about myself
answers.reply: Ooh. The best kind of surprise. Or the worst. Which?

answers.label: Something about someone
answers.reply: Careful with that one. Some surprises aren't ours to share.

answers.label: Nothing surprised me
answers.reply: Nothing! You must be very hard to surprise. I'll try harder.

asks: Someone leaves a sealed letter on a bench. Nobody's about. Do you peek?
A letter, left behind by the well. It isn't yours. Do you read it?

answers.label: Never
answers.reply: Never. You're right. Even I wouldn't. Probably.

answers.label: Just to find the owner
answers.reply: A peek for a good reason. That's what I'd tell myself, too.

answers.label: Take it to the post
answers.reply: The courier's office. Sensible and nosy-proof.

asks: Where's the line between curious and nosy?
When does asking questions turn into prying?

answers.label: When it hurts someone
answers.reply: Yes. I try to remember that. Not always well.

answers.label: When they ask you to stop
answers.reply: Clear and simple. A good rule.

answers.label: There isn't one
answers.reply: Ha! Dangerous answer. I like it, though.

asks: Have I ever been too nosy with you? Be honest. I can take it.
Do my questions ever bother you? Truly?

answers.label: Never
answers.reply: Never? Oh, good. I'll keep asking, then.

answers.label: Once or twice
answers.reply: Thank you for saying. I'll mind the line.

answers.label: A little, but I don't mind
answers.reply: A little. Ha. You're kind. I'll try to keep it to a little.

asks: Have you ever taken something apart just to see how it works?
Ever opened up a clock or a lock to look at the insides?

answers.label: Yes, and fixed it
answers.reply: Put back together and working? That's the dream.

answers.label: Yes, and broke it
answers.reply: Ha! The usual ending. Mine too. A drawer full of pieces.

answers.label: Never
answers.reply: Never! You've no idea what you're missing. Bring me something broken.

asks: Who's the one person you want to beat more than anybody?
Everyone's got someone they want to beat! Who's yours?

answers.label: My rival
answers.reply: Ha! Of course! Beat them, then beat them again!

answers.label: Myself from yesterday
answers.reply: Ooh. That's deep. And harder than any rival.

answers.label: Nobody, really
answers.reply: Nobody?! How do you get up in the morning?

answers.label: You
answers.reply: Ha! Then let's go! Training ground, right now!

asks: And when you finally beat them, what are you going to say?
The big win! The moment! What are your first words?

answers.label: "Good fight"
answers.reply: Gracious! I'd shout something. You're better than me.

answers.label: "Told you so"
answers.reply: Ha! YES! Exactly that!

answers.label: Nothing, just smile
answers.reply: Ooh, the silent smile. Cold. Brilliant.

answers.label: "Rematch!"
