answers.reply: Ha! Never stop! I love it!

asks: How spicy can you handle your food? I mean REALLY spicy!
The red pepper skewers at the festival! Can you take them?

answers.label: Bring it on
answers.reply: YES! The hottest stall at the festival! You and me!

answers.label: Mild, please
answers.reply: Mild! Ha! Fine, I'll eat the hot ones for both of us.

answers.label: Hotter than you
answers.reply: Oh, is that a challenge? It's a challenge!

asks: Is there ever a time to give up?
When things get really, really hard, do you ever just stop?

answers.label: Never!
answers.reply: NEVER! Ha! I knew you had it in you!

answers.label: Sometimes, yes
answers.reply: Sometimes? Hm. I hate it. But maybe you're right. Maybe.

answers.label: Only to start again
answers.reply: Ooh! Stop, catch your breath, and charge again! I like that!

asks: What's your biggest dream? Shout it! Go on, nobody's listening! Well, a few people.
Tell me your dream! Loud! Like you mean it!

answers.label: Hokage!
answers.reply: YES! Say it louder! The whole street heard that!

answers.label: The strongest shinobi!
answers.reply: Ha! A dream with teeth! I love it!

answers.label: To protect everyone!
answers.reply: Everyone! That's the biggest dream of all!

answers.label: I'd rather not shout
answers.reply: Oh. Fine. Whisper it then. I'll shout it for you.

asks: That dream! What's your first step, starting tomorrow? No, starting today!
Dreams need feet! What are you doing about yours, right now?

answers.label: Train at dawn
answers.reply: Dawn! I'll be there! We'll race the sun!

answers.label: Find a teacher
answers.reply: A teacher! Smart! I know a few loud ones.

answers.label: Already started
answers.reply: Already?! Ha! I'm late! Wait for me!

asks: Someone insults your friend right in front of you, in the street. What do you do?
Some loudmouth is mocking your friend at the market. Your move!

answers.label: Stand up to them
answers.reply: YES! Not with fists, though. Words first! Then maybe fists. No. Words.

answers.label: Walk away with my friend
answers.reply: Hm! Hard for me. But that's the bigger thing, isn't it?

answers.label: Make everyone laugh
answers.reply: Ha! Turn it on them with a joke! Clever!

asks: Is it better to show what you feel, or keep it in?
When you're angry or happy, do you let everyone see?

answers.label: Show it
answers.reply: Yes! Feelings are for feeling! Out loud!

answers.label: Keep it in
answers.reply: Keep it in? I'd burst! You're stronger than me.

answers.label: Depends on the moment
answers.reply: Ha. Fair. Even I keep quiet at a funeral. Mostly.

asks: When did you last feel something so big you couldn't hold it in?
Tell me about a time a feeling just burst right out of you!

answers.label: At a festival
answers.reply: The fireworks! Everyone screaming! Ha! The best feeling!

answers.label: In a fight
answers.reply: The fight! Heart pounding! Yes! I know that one!

answers.label: When a friend did well
answers.reply: Cheering for a friend! That's the best kind of shouting!

answers.label: Can't remember
answers.reply: Then we have to fix that! Let's go do something huge!

asks: What's the hardest training you've ever done? I bet I've done harder!
Your toughest drill! Tell me! I'll try to top it!

answers.label: A hundred laps
answers.reply: A hundred! Ha! I did a hundred and one! Just now!

answers.label: Under a waterfall
answers.reply: A waterfall! Freezing! Respect!

answers.label: Push-ups until dark
answers.reply: Until dark! YES! My arms hurt just hearing it!

answers.label: Nothing crazy
answers.reply: Nothing crazy?! Come train with me, then!

asks: Do you ever talk to animals? I do. I hope that's not strange.
The sparrows by my window know me by now. Do you have any animal friends?

answers.label: All the time
answers.reply: Oh, good. Then we're both a little strange.

answers.label: Only to stray cats
answers.reply: Strays need someone to talk to most of all.

answers.label: Not really
answers.reply: That's all right. Maybe one will choose you.

asks: Is there one animal in particular you're friends with? I'd love to meet them.
Tell me about your animal friend. Do they have a name?

answers.label: A stray cat
answers.reply: A stray. Oh. Do you feed it? Of course you feed it.

answers.label: Birds at my window
answers.reply: Birds! They remember faces, you know. They'll remember yours.

answers.label: Not yet
answers.reply: Not yet. When one chooses you, you'll know.

asks: Do you think harsh words ever help anyone?
Some teachers shout. Does it ever do any good?

answers.label: Sometimes
answers.reply: Sometimes. I suppose a loud word can wake someone up.

answers.label: Never
answers.reply: I think so too. There's always a softer way.

answers.label: Only from a friend
answers.reply: From someone who loves you. Yes. That's different.

asks: Do you have a favourite flower?
If I brought you a flower, which one would make you smile?

answers.label: Cherry blossom
answers.reply: Gone so quickly. That's what makes it precious.

answers.label: Sunflowers
answers.reply: Always turning to the light. That suits you.

answers.label: Morning glory
answers.reply: Opening at dawn, shy by noon. A lovely choice.

answers.label: Not really
answers.reply: That's all right. I'll find you one.

asks: You find a little bird with a hurt wing on the road. What do you do?
A sparrow with a broken wing, hopping in the lane. What would you do?

answers.label: Take it to the vet
answers.reply: The animal clinic by the kennels. They're so good. Yes.

answers.label: Nurse it myself
answers.reply: A box, soft cloth, a drop of water. You'd be a good nurse.

answers.label: Leave it to nature
answers.reply: Oh. Sometimes that's right, I know. It's still hard.

asks: And if the little bird got better, would you let it go, or keep it?
Say the wing heals. Do you open the box?

answers.label: Let it go
answers.reply: Yes. It belongs to the sky. Even if it hurts a bit to watch.

answers.label: Keep it safe
answers.reply: Safe with you. I understand. It would be loved.

answers.label: Let it choose
answers.reply: Open the window and let it decide. Oh, I like that best.

asks: Can someone be strong and gentle at the same time?
Do you think gentleness is a weakness, in a shinobi?

answers.label: Yes, of course
answers.reply: I hoped you'd say that.

answers.label: No, not really
answers.reply: Hm. I'd like to change your mind, one day. Gently.

answers.label: The strongest are
answers.reply: The strongest are the gentlest. Yes. I've seen it too.

asks: What's the kindest thing anyone's done for you here?
Is there a kindness someone showed you that you still think about?

answers.label: Someone fed me
answers.reply: A meal when you needed it. That's the oldest kindness.

answers.label: Someone listened
answers.reply: Listening. People forget how much that gives.

answers.label: Someone showed me around
answers.reply: Showing someone new the way. A lovely thing to do.

answers.label: Someone stood up for me
answers.reply: Oh. That takes courage. I'm glad someone was there.

asks: That kindness someone showed you. Did you ever get to thank them?
Have you told them what it meant to you?

answers.label: Yes, I did
answers.reply: Good. I'm sure it made their whole week.

answers.label: Not yet
answers.reply: There's still time. It doesn't have to be grand.

answers.label: I'm passing it on
answers.reply: Passing it on. That's the best thanks of all.

asks: Where in the village feels most peaceful to you?
When you need to feel calm, where do you go?

answers.label: The shrine
answers.reply: The bell and the cedar trees. Yes. It's so still there.

answers.label: The garden by the river
answers.reply: The little garden with the stone lantern? I love it too.

answers.label: My own window
answers.reply: Just your window and the sky. That's enough, isn't it?

answers.label: The flower shop
answers.reply: The Yamanaka shop. All those colours, and that smell. Lovely.

asks: If you were a colour, which colour would you be?
I think everyone has a colour. What's yours?

answers.label: Bright orange
answers.reply: Like a lantern at dusk. Yes, I can see it.

answers.label: Deep blue
answers.reply: The river at night. Calm and a little secret.

answers.label: Leaf green
answers.reply: The village's own colour. You belong here, then.

answers.label: All of them
answers.reply: A rainbow person! That's the best answer.

asks: Your colour. What does it feel like, from the inside?
If your colour were a feeling, what would it be?

answers.label: Like warmth
answers.reply: A warm colour from the inside. Like holding a teacup. Lovely.

answers.label: Like quiet
answers.reply: The quiet between two raindrops. I know that one.

answers.label: Like the open air
answers.reply: A colour with the sky in it. That's you exactly.

answers.label: It just is
answers.reply: Ha! Colours don't need reasons. You're right.

asks: Look at that cloud. What does it look like to you?
That one, just over the Hokage Rock. What do you see?

answers.label: A dragon
answers.reply: A dragon! With a curly tail, look. You've a good eye.

answers.label: A bowl of ramen
answers.reply: Ha! Noodles and all. Are you hungry? You're hungry.

answers.label: A sleeping cat
answers.reply: Curled up on the sky's lap. Oh, that's sweet.

answers.label: Just a cloud
answers.reply: Just a cloud. Ha! Keep your feet on the ground for both of us.

asks: If you could become any animal for a day, which would you be?
One day as an animal. Which one, and what would you do?

answers.label: A hawk
answers.reply: The whole village from above! You'd have to tell me what the rooftops look like.

answers.label: A fish
answers.reply: Under the river, all green light and quiet. How peaceful.

answers.label: A fox
answers.reply: Sly and quick. Ha. I can see you with a bushy tail.

answers.label: A lazy cat
answers.reply: A day of sunbeams. The wisest choice of all.

asks: Do you think dreams mean anything?
When you dream, is it your heart talking, or just your supper?

answers.label: Yes, they do
answers.reply: I think so too. Mine are always trying to tell me something. In riddles.

answers.label: No, just supper
answers.reply: Ha! Too much pickled radish before bed. Maybe you're right.

answers.label: Only the good ones
answers.reply: Clever! Keep the good, forget the rest.

asks: What did you dream last night? Tell me everything.
Tell me a dream you've had lately. The stranger the better.

answers.label: Flying
answers.reply: Over the rooftops! The best dream there is.

answers.label: Falling
answers.reply: Ooh. Everyone has that one. You always wake before the end.

answers.label: Food. Lots of food
answers.reply: Ha! Your supper was talking. A feast dream is a good omen, I've decided.

answers.label: I don't remember
answers.reply: Gone with the morning. Keep a brush by your bed.

asks: If you painted the village, what would you paint first?
One painting of the Leaf. What's in it?

answers.label: The Hokage Rock
answers.reply: The great faces in morning light. Ambitious.

answers.label: The river at sunset
answers.reply: Orange water and the bridges black against it. Oh, yes.

answers.label: The market crowds
answers.reply: All those faces and colours! You'd need a very big scroll.

answers.label: My window's view
answers.reply: The view you see every day. That's the truest painting.

asks: If someone wrote a story about you, what would it be called?
Your life as a scroll on the shop shelf. What's the title?

answers.label: Never Giving Up
answers.reply: A good title. I'd buy it.

answers.label: The Quiet One
answers.reply: Mysterious. Readers love a quiet hero.

answers.label: Ramen and Glory
answers.reply: Ha! A comedy. I'd buy two copies.

answers.label: Not written yet
answers.reply: Of course. You're still in the first chapters.

asks: And your story. How should it end?
The last page of your scroll. What's on it?

answers.label: Happily
answers.reply: Happily. The best stories earn it.

answers.label: A new beginning
answers.reply: Ah, the kind that closes one door and opens another. Lovely.

answers.label: It never ends
answers.reply: Ha! A story that goes on and on. The best kind.

asks: Should art have rules?
The old masters had a hundred rules for painting a crane. Should we follow them?

answers.label: Some, yes
answers.reply: The rules hold the brush steady. Fair.

answers.label: None at all
answers.reply: Paint the crane purple! Yes!

answers.label: Learn them, then break them
answers.reply: The old painters' secret. You've found it.

asks: Do you fold your clothes at night, or drop them on a chair?
Be honest: at night, do your clothes get folded, or flung?

answers.label: Folded, always
answers.reply: Good. Order at home, order on a mission.

answers.label: On a chair
answers.reply: The chair. Of course it's the chair. We'll work on it.

answers.label: Somewhere in between
answers.reply: Folded on good days. A fair answer, I suppose.

asks: And your tool pouch? What's in it, and in what order?
Talk me through your tool pouch, front to back. I'm curious. Professionally.

answers.label: Kunai left, shuriken right
answers.reply: A system! Wire at the back, I hope. Excellent.

answers.label: Whatever fits
answers.reply: Whatever fits. I felt that in my teeth.

answers.label: Snacks first
answers.reply: Snacks first. Priorities are a kind of order, I suppose.

asks: Is five minutes late really late?
Somebody turns up five minutes after the agreed time. Late, or fine?

answers.label: Yes, late is late
answers.reply: Thank you. Finally. Someone understands.

answers.label: Five minutes is fine
answers.reply: Five minutes is three hundred seconds. I counted. Every one.

answers.label: Depends on the occasion
answers.reply: A fair distinction. A mission, never. Tea, perhaps.

asks: When someone's late, what do you assume first?
A friend doesn't arrive on time. Where does your mind go?

answers.label: Something happened
answers.reply: Kind of you. I usually assume carelessness. I'll try your way.

answers.label: They don't care
answers.reply: Harsh, but sometimes accurate. I've thought it too.

answers.label: They lost track of time
answers.reply: Most likely. A sundial would fix it. I've suggested this to several people.

asks: Do you plan your day, or see where it goes?
A list every morning, or wherever the wind takes you?

answers.label: A list every morning
answers.reply: A list! Do you number it? I number mine.

answers.label: See where it goes
answers.reply: Where it goes. Remarkable. I'd need a lie down.

answers.label: A rough plan
answers.reply: A rough plan is still a plan. Acceptable.

asks: You notice a picture hanging crooked in someone else's house. Do you straighten it?
A friend's scroll is hanging crooked on their wall. What do you do?

answers.label: Straighten it
answers.reply: Yes. Immediately. It's a kindness, really.

answers.label: Mention it
answers.reply: Politely. Good. They can straighten it themselves.

answers.label: Leave it
answers.reply: Leave it. I couldn't. I'd think about it for days.

asks: Is "good enough" ever good enough?
Do you finish a job when it works, or when it's right?

answers.label: Sometimes
answers.reply: Sometimes. I'm trying to learn that. It's hard.

answers.label: Never
answers.reply: Never. A kindred spirit. Our work will outlast us both.

answers.label: For chores, yes
answers.reply: Chores, yes. Kunai, no. A reasonable line.

asks: Have you ever spent so long perfecting something that you missed the moment for it?
I once polished a gift so long I missed the birthday. Has anything like that happened to you?

answers.label: Yes, once
answers.reply: Then you understand. It stings, doesn't it?

answers.label: No, never
answers.reply: Good. Keep it that way. Set a deadline. Write it down.

answers.label: I rush instead
answers.reply: The opposite problem! Perhaps we balance each other out.

asks: Your desk at home: tidy, or creative chaos?
If I looked at your table right now, what would I find?

answers.label: Tidy
answers.reply: Brushes in a row? Ink capped? I'm very pleased.

answers.label: Creative chaos
answers.reply: Chaos. I'll pretend I didn't hear. For our friendship.

answers.label: Tidy on top, messy drawers
answers.reply: Ha. The drawer is where order goes to die. I know it well.

asks: My shop ledger's in a muddle. Fix it tonight, or wait for my day off?
My accounts are three days behind. All of them. Advise me.

answers.label: Tonight
answers.reply: Tonight. Yes. I won't sleep otherwise anyway.

answers.label: On your day off
answers.reply: Rest first, then sums. Sensible. Painful, but sensible.

answers.label: A little each evening
answers.reply: Ten lines a night. A schedule! You understand me.

asks: Truth or dare? Quick, no thinking!
Pick one, fast: truth or dare?

answers.label: Truth
answers.reply: Ha! Then tell me your most embarrassing training accident. Later. Tonight.

answers.label: Dare
answers.reply: Dare! Ring the shrine bell at midnight. Kidding. Mostly.

answers.label: Neither, I'm leaving
answers.reply: Ha! Chicken! Bwak bwak!

asks: Truth or dare, round two! Bigger stakes this time. Same pick?
Rematch! Truth or dare, and no running off this time!

answers.label: Truth again
answers.reply: Fine! Who's the funniest person in the village? Besides me.

answers.label: Dare again
answers.reply: Ha! Walk backwards to the noodle stand and order in a whisper. Go!

answers.label: Switch it up
answers.reply: Unpredictable! I love it. I'll think of something terrible.

asks: What's the best game ever invented? Wrong answers only. No, right answers. Go.
Tag, hide and seek, shogi: what's the greatest game there is?

answers.label: Tag
answers.reply: Classic! You're it. Ha, got you.

answers.label: Hide and seek
answers.reply: Ninja hide and seek! Takes hours. Sometimes days.

answers.label: Shogi
answers.reply: Ooh, a thinker. I'm terrible at it. Teach me?

answers.label: Kick the can
answers.reply: Ha! The old street game! Nobody plays it anymore. Let's revive it.

asks: Is it cheating to use a jutsu in hide and seek?
Using clones in a game of tag: fair play or cheating?

answers.label: Totally fair
answers.reply: Ha! Then you'll never find me. I can turn into a bush.

answers.label: Cheating!
answers.reply: A purist! Fine, no jutsu. Just legs and cunning.

answers.label: Only clones are fair
answers.reply: Ha! A whole rulebook in one sentence. I accept.

asks: If you could prank anyone in the village and get away with it, who would it be?
One perfect prank, no consequences. Who's the target?

answers.label: My sensei
answers.reply: Ha! Brave, brave, brave. I'd help. From a safe distance.

answers.label: The gate guards
answers.reply: They stand still so long! They'd never see it coming.

answers.label: Lord Hokage
answers.reply: Ha! The ultimate prank. Legends are made this way. Or careers end.

answers.label: Nobody, I'm good
answers.reply: Nobody? I'll make a prankster of you yet.

asks: Your perfect prank. How would you do it? Spill the plan.
All right, the prank. Walk me through it. I won't tell. Probably.

answers.label: Clones everywhere
answers.reply: Fifty of you, all waving. Ha! Chaos. Beautiful chaos.

answers.label: Paint, lots of paint
answers.reply: Something bright and harmless. It washes off. Eventually.

answers.label: Bucket over the door
answers.reply: The classics never fail. Respect.

asks: Race you to the end of the street! Wait, do you even like racing?
First one to the bridge wins! Unless you're not a racer?

answers.label: Love it
answers.reply: Ha! Ready, set... I'm already gone!

answers.label: I'd rather stroll
answers.reply: A stroller! Fine, I'll race you there and back, you walk.

answers.label: Only if I win
answers.reply: Ha! Then I'll give you a head start. Three steps.

asks: Do you think grown-ups forget how to have fun?
Why do people get so serious as they get older?

answers.label: Yes, mostly
answers.reply: Not me! I refuse. I'll be spinning tops at ninety.

answers.label: No, they hide it
answers.reply: Ha! Secret fun. Like the elders playing cards behind the shrine.

answers.label: Not you, anyway
answers.reply: Ha! Best compliment I've had all week.

asks: Would you wear a silly hat all day for a hundred ryo?
A hundred ryo to wear a ridiculous hat from dawn to dusk. Deal?

answers.label: Yes, easy
answers.reply: Ha! Easy ryo. I'll find the silliest one in the market.

answers.label: For two hundred
answers.reply: A negotiator! Fine. Two hundred, and it has feathers.

answers.label: I'd wear it for free
answers.reply: Ha! That's the spirit. You're my favourite.

asks: Raising the stakes: a hat shaped like a fish. For the whole festival.
The fish hat. Full festival. Everyone watching. Still brave?

answers.label: Done
answers.reply: Ha! Legend. I'm telling everyone.

answers.label: Absolutely not
answers.reply: Even you have limits! I knew it.

answers.label: Only if you wear one too
answers.reply: Ha! Matching fish hats. It's a deal. Shake on it.

asks: Say you had a thousand ryo, all at once. What would you do with it?
A thousand ryo lands in your lap. Spend it, save it, or invest it?

answers.label: Save it
answers.reply: Good. A thousand saved is two thousand later, if you're patient.

answers.label: Better gear
answers.reply: A sound investment. Good tools save lives.

answers.label: Treat my friends
answers.reply: Generous. Not the best return, but a fine one.

answers.label: Ramen, for a year
answers.reply: Ha! Three hundred bowls. I did the sums.

asks: Spent any ryo lately you regret? I won't judge. Much.
What's the worst thing you've ever spent money on?

answers.label: Too many sweets
answers.reply: Sweets. The silent purse-thief. Everyone's weakness.

answers.label: Nothing, I'm careful
answers.reply: Careful! I knew I liked you.

answers.label: A gift nobody liked
answers.reply: Ouch. Well, the thought had value. The gift, less so.

asks: Is anything worth paying double for?
What's one thing you'd never buy cheap?

answers.label: Good tools
answers.reply: Agreed. A cheap kunai costs twice: once to buy, once to replace.

answers.label: Good food
answers.reply: Fair. You are what you eat, and I'd rather be good rice.

answers.label: Nothing, ever
answers.reply: Ha! A hard bargainer. The market fears you.

answers.label: Time with friends
answers.reply: Time's not for sale. But if it were, yes. Good answer.

asks: Cheap kunai that might snap, or good ones that cost a week's pay?
The Hagane forge or the bargain bin: where do you buy your kunai?

answers.label: The good ones
answers.reply: Sensible. The Hagane charge for a reason.

answers.label: The cheap ones
answers.reply: Hm. Carry spares, then. Lots of spares.

answers.label: Borrow and make do
answers.reply: Ha! The cheapest of all. Mind you give them back.

asks: Hard work or clever work: which gets you further?
Graft or wits? Which one pays better in the long run?

answers.label: Hard work
answers.reply: Steady work never goes out of fashion. True.

answers.label: Clever work
answers.reply: Work smarter. The best merchants agree with you.

answers.label: Both, together
answers.reply: Ha! The full ledger. You'll go far.

asks: Ever found a clever shortcut that turned out badly?
Has a smart idea of yours ever cost more than it saved?

answers.label: Yes, once
answers.reply: Once is tuition. Twice is carelessness. You've paid your tuition.

answers.label: Never
answers.reply: Never? Then you haven't tried enough shortcuts. Ha.

answers.label: All the time
answers.reply: Ha! At least you're consistent.

asks: Do you save any of your mission pay?
When the Mission Desk pays you, where does the ryo go?

answers.label: Half, at least
answers.reply: Half! Remarkable discipline. You'll own a house before me.

answers.label: A little
answers.reply: A little is far better than none. Keep at it.

answers.label: I spend it all
answers.reply: All of it? Hm. We'll talk.

asks: What are you saving towards, then?
Saving's easier with a goal. What's yours?

answers.label: Better gear
answers.reply: An investment in staying alive. The best kind.

answers.label: A home someday
answers.reply: A home of your own. That's worth every ryo.

answers.label: Just in case
answers.reply: The rainy-day fund. Wise. Rain always comes.

answers.label: A gift for someone
answers.reply: Saving for someone else. That's a different kind of rich.

asks: Rice costs more this year. Do I raise my prices, or swallow the cost?
My costs are up. My regulars are poor. Raise prices or not?

answers.label: Raise them
answers.reply: Business is business. You're right. I'll grit my teeth and do it.

answers.label: Swallow the cost
answers.reply: For a season, maybe. For my regulars. Hm. Kind of you.

answers.label: A little, and explain
answers.reply: A sign by the till: "Rice is dear this year." Honest and fair. Good.

asks: People who brag about their missions. Annoying, or fair enough?
A Genin tells you about the same C-rank for the fourth time. Your reaction?

answers.label: Annoying
answers.reply: Agreed. Talk is cheap. Results aren't.

answers.label: Fair, if it's true
answers.reply: True bragging is just reporting. Loudly. Fair.

answers.label: Fun to listen to
answers.reply: Ha! You're kinder than me.

asks: Did you get home all right last night? The lanes are dark after the lanterns go out.
You were out late. Home safe? Tell me you took the lit streets.

answers.label: Yes, safe and sound
answers.reply: Good. That's all I needed to hear.

answers.label: I took the long way
answers.reply: The long way's the lit way. Smart.

answers.label: I stayed out very late
answers.reply: Very late. Hm. Next time, send word. Humour me.

asks: Is it brave or reckless to fight someone stronger, to protect a friend?
A friend in trouble, an enemy who outclasses you. Is stepping in brave, or foolish?

answers.label: Brave
answers.reply: Brave. I'd do it too. I'd hate you doing it.

answers.label: Reckless. Get help
answers.reply: Yes. Run for help, fast. That's not cowardice, that's sense.

answers.label: Both, and worth it
answers.reply: Both. Ha. That's the honest answer.

asks: Would you, though? Really step in front of a friend?
If it came to it, would you put yourself between a friend and harm?

answers.label: Without thinking
answers.reply: Without thinking. I believe you. I'll worry about you forever now.

answers.label: If I had to
answers.reply: If you had to. That's the steadiest answer. Good.

answers.label: I'd find a smarter way
answers.reply: A smarter way. Good. The best protectors think first.

asks: What do you always carry, just in case?
When you leave the house, what's in your pocket for emergencies?

answers.label: Bandages
answers.reply: Good. I carry two rolls. You can never have enough.

answers.label: A spare kunai
answers.reply: Sensible. Keep it sharp.

answers.label: A snack
answers.reply: Ha! An emergency snack. That's survival, too.

answers.label: Nothing at all
answers.reply: Nothing! Here. Take a bandage. And a whistle. Don't argue.

asks: Who do you feel you have to protect?
Is there anyone you'd always look out for, no matter what?

answers.label: My squad
answers.reply: As it should be. Watch their backs. They'll watch yours.

answers.label: The little ones
answers.reply: The children. Yes. They're the whole village's to protect.

answers.label: Everyone
answers.reply: Everyone. That's a heavy load. Share it.

answers.label: Myself first
answers.reply: Yourself first. Good. You can't protect anyone flat on your back.

asks: And who protects you?
You watch over others. Who watches over you?

answers.label: My friends
answers.reply: Good friends. Keep them close.

answers.label: My sensei
answers.reply: A good sensei is a good shield.

answers.label: I protect myself
answers.reply: You do. But you don't have to do it alone.

answers.label: Maybe you do
answers.reply: ...Yes. I'd like to. I will.

asks: Your friend wants to do something dangerous. Stop them, or let them choose?
A friend's set on a risky climb up the cliffs. What do you do?

answers.label: Stop them
answers.reply: Even if they're cross with you. Yes. Better cross than hurt.

answers.label: Let them choose
answers.reply: Their life, their choice. It's hard. You're right, though.

answers.label: Go with them
answers.reply: Go with them. Then at least you're there. That's what I'd do.

asks: My nephew's on missions now. I lie awake every night. How do I stop worrying?
Someone I love is out on the roads with a squad. How do I sleep?

answers.label: Trust their training
answers.reply: Trust the Academy. Trust the sensei. Yes. I'll try.

answers.label: Keep yourself busy
answers.reply: Busy hands, quiet mind. I'll clean the whole house twice.

answers.label: Write to them
answers.reply: Letters! Something for them to come home to. Lovely.

answers.label: You can't. That's love
answers.reply: Ha. You're right. I'll stop trying to stop.

asks: My nephew came home safe! Should I tell them how much I worried?
They're home. Do I tell them about the sleepless nights?

answers.label: Yes, tell them
answers.reply: You're right. They should know someone was waiting.

answers.label: No. Just feed them
answers.reply: Ha! Feed them and fuss. That says it all anyway.

answers.label: Just a little
answers.reply: A little. Enough that they know. Not so much they feel guilty. Wise.

asks: Have you ever thought about joining the village guard one day?
The gate, the walls, the night watch. Could you see yourself there?

answers.label: Yes, I'd like that
answers.reply: Good. The village sleeps easier with people like you on the walls.

answers.label: No, missions for me
answers.reply: The road calls you. Fair. Come back safe, every time.

answers.label: Maybe, later
answers.reply: Later. When you've seen enough roads. That's how most guards start.

asks: Is second place worth anything?
You come second in a contest. Is that something to be pleased about?

answers.label: Nothing at all
answers.reply: Exactly. Second is the first loser. ...I'm only half joking.

answers.label: It's a step
answers.reply: A step. Hm. Fine. As long as you keep climbing.

answers.label: Depends who won
answers.reply: Ha. Losing to a master is no shame. Losing to a fool is.

asks: Who would you hate most to lose to?
There's always one person you can't bear to lose to. Who's yours?

answers.label: My rival
answers.reply: Of course. That's what rivals are for. Don't let them.

answers.label: A friend
answers.reply: A friend. That's the one that stings. I know.

answers.label: Nobody. Losing is losing
answers.reply: Hm. Fair. It's all the same to the scoreboard.

asks: Should a name be carried with pride, even when the family behind it has made mistakes?
Do you think a name is something you inherit, or something you earn?

answers.label: Carry it with pride
answers.reply: Yes. A name is a promise to the ones before you.

answers.label: It's what you make it
answers.reply: Your own name, your own deeds. I can't argue.

answers.label: Pride must be earned
answers.reply: Earned. Yes. Even mine. Especially mine.

asks: What will you be the best in the village at, one day?
Every shinobi should aim to be the best at something. What's yours?

answers.label: Taijutsu
answers.reply: Hand to hand. The purest test. A worthy aim.

answers.label: Ninjutsu
answers.reply: Techniques. Hm. You'll need control as well as power.

answers.label: Strategy
answers.reply: The mind. The rarest kind of strength.

answers.label: I don't need to be best
answers.reply: ...Hm. A strange answer. Perhaps a wise one. I'll think on it.

asks: And how will you get there? Specifics. I want a plan.
Being best takes more than wanting. What's your plan?

answers.label: Train twice as hard
answers.reply: Twice as hard as whom? Everyone. Good.

answers.label: Find a master
answers.reply: A master. Yes. Pride shouldn't stop you learning.

answers.label: Learn from losing
answers.reply: From losing. Hm. You're wiser than I was.

asks: Do you like being praised?
When someone tells you you've done well, how does it feel?

answers.label: Yes, I do
answers.reply: Honest. Most pretend otherwise. I do.

answers.label: It embarrasses me
answers.reply: Hm. Learn to take it. You've earned it more than you think.

answers.label: Only when it's earned
answers.reply: Exactly. Cheap praise is worse than none.

asks: Your rival asks you for help with a technique. Do you help?
The one person you most want to beat asks for your advice. What do you say?

answers.label: Yes, I'd help
answers.reply: Generous. A strong rival makes you stronger. ...Annoyingly true.

answers.label: No, never
answers.reply: Ha! At least you're honest about it.

answers.label: Help, then beat them
answers.reply: Ha! Yes. That's the proper way.

asks: Is it hard for you to say sorry?
Some people choke on the word "sorry". Do you?

answers.label: Yes, very
answers.reply: ...Same. Don't tell anyone.

answers.label: No, it's easy
answers.reply: Easy? Hm. Teach me sometime. Quietly.

answers.label: Only when I'm right
answers.reply: Ha! When you're right it's hardest of all.

asks: When did you last say sorry and truly mean it?
Your last real apology. Do you remember it?

answers.label: Not long ago
answers.reply: Good. Keep the habit. I'm... trying to, too.

answers.label: I can't remember
answers.reply: Then it's been too long. For both of us, perhaps.

answers.label: I'd rather not say
answers.reply: Fine. Pride keeps its own counsel. I know.

asks: What do you hold to the highest standard: your training, your word, or how you look?
Where will you never cut corners?

answers.label: My training
answers.reply: Good. Sloppy training makes sloppy shinobi.

answers.label: My word
answers.reply: Your word. The one thing nobody can take. Correct.

answers.label: How I look
answers.reply: Ha. A clean vest is a kind of discipline. I won't mock it.

answers.label: I'm relaxed about it
answers.reply: Relaxed. Hm. I'll have to work on you.

asks: Quiet company, or chatter?
Do you like people who talk, or people who don't?

answers.label: Quiet company
answers.reply: Good. ...This is nice, then.

answers.label: Chatter
answers.reply: Hm. I'll try to keep up. No promises.

answers.label: Depends who
answers.reply: Fair. Some silences are better than others.

asks: Some things should stay private. Agree?
Do you think people share too much?

answers.label: Yes
answers.reply: Yes. Good.

answers.label: No, share more
answers.reply: Hm. Maybe that works for you.

answers.label: With the right person
answers.reply: The right person. ...Yes. That's the exception.

asks: Is there something you've never told anyone? Don't tell me. Just yes or no.
A thing you've kept to yourself, always. Do you have one? Only yes or no.

answers.label: Yes
answers.reply: Thought so. So do I. We'll leave it there.

answers.label: No
answers.reply: Lucky. Or very open. Either way.

answers.label: Maybe
answers.reply: Maybe. A good answer.

asks: Where do you go when you want to be alone?
Everyone needs somewhere to disappear. Yours?

answers.label: My apartment
answers.reply: Door shut. Simple.

answers.label: The forest edge
answers.reply: Good choice. Nobody follows you there.

answers.label: The library
answers.reply: The back shelves. Nobody talks. I know the spot.

answers.label: I don't, really
answers.reply: You don't? Hm. Strange. I envy it, a little.

asks: Small talk. Pointless?
Weather, prices, who's ill. Do you enjoy that sort of talk?

answers.label: Pointless
answers.reply: Agreed. ...Nice weather, though. Ha.

answers.label: It's useful
answers.reply: Oil for the hinges. Fine. I'll grant you that.

answers.label: Nice, sometimes
answers.reply: Sometimes. With the right baker.

asks: Tea. How do you take it?
Green tea, plain? Or something else?

answers.label: Plain green
answers.reply: Correct.

answers.label: Sweetened
answers.reply: Sweet tea. Hm. Your business.

answers.label: I don't drink it
answers.reply: No tea at all. I'll remember.

asks: ...I make decent tea. Would you drink some? With me?
I've a pot on. You can stay. If you like.

answers.label: Yes, please
answers.reply: Good. Sit. Don't talk for a bit. It's better that way.

answers.label: If you're having some
answers.reply: I am. Two cups, then.

answers.label: Another time
answers.reply: Another time. The offer stands.

asks: People who pry. How do you deal with them?
Someone keeps asking you personal questions. What do you do?

answers.label: Change the subject
answers.reply: Weather. Works every time.

answers.label: Tell them plainly
answers.reply: "That's mine." Simple. Good.

answers.label: Answer politely
answers.reply: Patient. More patient than me.

asks: Do you trust people quickly, or slowly?
How long before you trust someone?

answers.label: Quickly
answers.reply: Quickly. Brave. Or reckless. Hm.

answers.label: Slowly
answers.reply: Slowly. Me too. It lasts longer that way.

answers.label: It depends
answers.reply: On the person. Obviously. Fair.

asks: ...And me? Do you trust me yet?
Just asking. Do you trust me?

answers.label: Yes
answers.reply: ...Good. That's good.

answers.label: Getting there
answers.reply: Getting there. Fair. So am I.

answers.label: Not yet
answers.reply: Not yet. Honest. I respect it.

asks: Um... what do you like doing, when it's quiet?
When there's nobody around... what do you do?

answers.label: Reading
answers.reply: Oh! Me too. I... I could lend you something. If you want.

answers.label: Drawing
answers.reply: Drawing? I... I draw too. A little.

answers.label: Long walks
answers.reply: Walks are nice. Nobody expects you to talk.

answers.label: Napping
answers.reply: Ha... yes. Naps are the best quiet thing.

asks: Do you think... small brave things count? Like, really count?
Is it still brave if it's only a little thing?

answers.label: Yes, the most
answers.reply: Oh. That's... thank you. I needed that.

answers.label: Big ones matter more
answers.reply: Oh. Maybe. Big ones start small, though. Don't they?

answers.label: All of them count
answers.reply: All of them. Okay. I'll... count mine, then.

asks: What's a small brave thing you've done? You don't have to... I just wondered.
Can you tell me about a time you were brave? Even a tiny bit?

answers.label: Spoke up in class
answers.reply: In front of everyone? Wow. I could never. Not yet.

answers.label: Made a new friend
answers.reply: That's the scariest one, I think. You're very brave.

answers.label: Tried something new
answers.reply: New things... yes. My hands shake just thinking about it.

answers.label: I can't think of one
answers.reply: That's okay. I think... talking to me counts. A bit.

asks: Do crowds... bother you? Like on Market Day?
Is it just me, or are festivals very... loud?

answers.label: Yes, a bit
answers.reply: Oh good. I mean, not good. But... I'm not the only one.

answers.label: No, I like them
answers.reply: You like them? Maybe... I could stand next to you, next time.

answers.label: With a friend, they're fine
answers.reply: With a friend. Yes. That helps. That helps a lot.

asks: If you knew the answer in class, but you were scared... would you still say it?
Hand up, or keep quiet? When you know, but everyone's looking?

answers.label: Yes, I'd say it
answers.reply: Even with everyone looking? You're... really brave.

answers.label: I'd whisper to a friend
answers.reply: Oh. That's what I do. Then they say it.

answers.label: No, I'd keep quiet
answers.reply: Me too. Usually. Maybe we can... both try. Sometime.

asks: Could you... help me practise speaking up? What should I say first?
If I wanted to be braver at talking to people, where would I even start?

answers.label: Just say hello
answers.reply: Hello. Okay. Hello. ...Hello! I did it.

answers.label: Ask one question
answers.reply: One question. "Is this seat free?" I can... I can do that.

answers.label: Just say your name
answers.reply: My name. Out loud. To a stranger. ...Next week.

asks: I draw sometimes. Um. Do you make anything?
Do you... make things? With your hands, I mean?

answers.label: I draw too
answers.reply: You do? Could we... draw together? Sometime? Not now. Sometime.

answers.label: I cook
answers.reply: Cooking is making too. The best kind. You can eat it.

answers.label: I write things down
answers.reply: Writing. I'd... like to read it. If you'd let me.

answers.label: Not really
answers.reply: That's okay. Watching is nice too.

asks: Can quiet people be good friends? Even if they don't say much?
Do you think a friend has to talk a lot?

answers.label: The very best
answers.reply: Oh. I... I'll remember you said that.

answers.label: Yes, of course
answers.reply: Of course. Okay. I always wondered.

answers.label: Talking doesn't matter
answers.reply: Not talking is fine? Oh, good. That's... a relief.

asks: Are we... friends? I mean, would you say we are?
Can I ask... do you think of me as a friend?

answers.label: Yes, of course
answers.reply: Oh! Oh. Okay. I... I'm going to remember this.

answers.label: Good friends
answers.reply: Good friends. ...I'm smiling. Sorry. I can't stop.

answers.label: Getting there
answers.reply: Getting there. That's... that's still good. Yes.

asks: Do you remember the first time we spoke? I was so nervous.
The first time we talked... did I seem strange? I felt strange.

answers.label: Yes, I remember
answers.reply: You do? Oh no. Ha. I mean... oh, that's nice.

answers.label: Not really, sorry
answers.reply: That's okay! Actually... that's a relief.

answers.label: I was nervous too
answers.reply: You were? Really? Oh. That makes it so much better.

asks: What's the hardest promise you've ever kept?
Have you ever kept your word when it cost you?

answers.label: A small one that cost a lot
answers.reply: The small ones are the true test. Nobody's watching.

answers.label: None that hard yet
answers.reply: Then you've a clean record. Keep it that way.

answers.label: I'd rather not say
answers.reply: Fair. A kept promise doesn't need telling.

asks: When duty and what you want pull different ways, which one wins?
Your duty says one thing, your heart another. Which do you follow?

answers.label: Duty
answers.reply: Duty. Plain and simple. Not easy, but simple.

answers.label: What I want
answers.reply: Hm. Honest, at least. Just be sure you can live with it.

answers.label: It depends
answers.reply: On what's at stake. Fair. I'd say the same, if pressed.

asks: Has duty ever cost you something you wanted?
Have you ever given up something you wanted because you'd said you'd do a job?

answers.label: Yes, it did
answers.reply: I'm sorry. And I'm proud of you. Both can be true.

answers.label: Not yet
answers.reply: It will, one day. When it does, you'll know what you're made of.

answers.label: And I'd do it again
answers.reply: That's the steel. You'll make a fine shinobi.

asks: Do you keep to the same routine every day?
Same breakfast, same path, same time? Or different each day?

answers.label: Yes, every day
answers.reply: Good. Routine is a rope you can hold in the dark.

answers.label: No, I like variety
answers.reply: Variety. Fair enough. Keep one thing steady, though.

answers.label: Mostly
answers.reply: Mostly is honest. Most of us are mostly.

asks: A friend asks you to cover their shift, but you're exhausted. Do you?
You're dead on your feet, and a friend needs someone to stand in for them. Yes or no?

answers.label: Yes, I'll do it
answers.reply: A friend asked. That settles it. Get a strong tea first.

answers.label: No, I need rest
answers.reply: Honest. A tired guard is half a guard. You're right.

answers.label: I'll find someone else
answers.reply: Solve it without breaking yourself. Good thinking.

asks: Who in your life do you rely on most?
When it counts, who do you lean on?

answers.label: My squad
answers.reply: As it should be. A squad that leans together stands.

answers.label: My teacher
answers.reply: A good teacher is a good wall to lean on.

answers.label: Myself
answers.reply: Yourself. Strong. Just don't make it only yourself.

answers.label: A good friend
answers.reply: One good friend is worth a hundred acquaintances.

asks: And who relies on you?
Turn it around. Who leans on you when it counts?

answers.label: My squad does
answers.reply: Then carry it well. You will.

answers.label: No one yet
answers.reply: They will. Be ready.

answers.label: More than I know
answers.reply: Ha. That's usually the truth for good people.

asks: If you made the Leaf one promise, what would it be?
One promise to the whole village. What do you swear?

answers.label: I'll protect it
answers.reply: A shinobi's oath. Said plainly. Good.

answers.label: I'll never leave
answers.reply: Never is a long word. But I believe you mean it.

answers.label: I'll make it proud
answers.reply: Proud. Yes. That one we can all see you keep.

asks: That promise to the Leaf. How do you keep it, day to day?
Big promises are kept in small days. What does yours look like on a Tuesday?

answers.label: Training every day
answers.reply: Every day. Rain or shine. That's how.

answers.label: Helping where I can
answers.reply: A hand here, an errand there. That's a promise kept quietly.

answers.label: Showing up
answers.reply: Showing up. Half of duty is just being there. Well said.

asks: Should you be honest with a friend, even when it'll hurt them?
A friend asks you a straight question, and the true answer will sting. Do you give it?

answers.label: Yes, always
answers.reply: Straight is kindest in the long run. I agree.

answers.label: No, spare them
answers.reply: Kindness first. I see it. I'm not sure I could.

answers.label: Honest, but gently
answers.reply: The truth, wrapped in care. That's the right way.

asks: Do you train when no one is watching?
When your sensei isn't there to check, do you still do the drills?

answers.label: Every day
answers.reply: Good. Discipline is what you do when no one is counting.

answers.label: When I feel like it
answers.reply: Then you'll be strong when you feel like it. Think on that.

answers.label: I do my own drills
answers.reply: Your own way. Acceptable, if you do them.

asks: When did you last skip training? Answer honestly.
The last time you missed a session. When was it, and why?

answers.label: This week
answers.reply: Honest. Don't make it two weeks.

answers.label: Never
answers.reply: Never. Hm. Good. Don't let it start.

answers.label: I don't remember
answers.reply: Then it was too long ago to matter, or too often to count. Which?

asks: Discipline or talent. Which matters more?
A gifted student who coasts, or an ordinary one who never stops. Who goes further?

answers.label: Discipline
answers.reply: Correct. Talent is a loan. Discipline is the interest.

answers.label: Talent
answers.reply: Wrong, mostly. But talent with discipline is unstoppable.

answers.label: Discipline, in time
answers.reply: Exactly. Talent wins early. Discipline wins late. Late is longer.

asks: What is your greatest weakness as a shinobi?
Name your weakest point. No modesty, no excuses.

answers.label: Patience
answers.reply: Patience. Train it like a muscle. Sit still for ten minutes a day.

answers.label: Chakra control
answers.reply: Control. Leaf-balancing, every night. No shortcuts.

answers.label: My guard
answers.reply: Your guard. I've seen it drop. Fix it.

answers.label: I don't know yet
answers.reply: Then find out before an enemy does.

asks: That weakness. What are you doing about it?
You named your weakness. Now: what's the plan?

answers.label: Drilling it daily
answers.reply: Daily. Good. Report back in a month.

answers.label: Asking for help
answers.reply: Wise. Pride is the second weakness. You've beaten that one.

answers.label: Nothing yet
answers.reply: Nothing. Start tomorrow. At dawn.

asks: Your captain gives an order you believe is wrong. What do you do?
An order from above, and you're sure it's a mistake. Obey?

answers.label: Obey
answers.reply: Obey. Then ask afterwards. A squad that argues mid-mission loses.

answers.label: Question it at once
answers.reply: Speak up. Quickly, clearly, once. Then do as you're told.

answers.label: Obey, then report it
answers.reply: Correct. The chain exists for a reason. Use it.

asks: Is lateness a small fault?
Someone is always a little late. Does it matter?

answers.label: Yes, a small one
answers.reply: Small faults grow. Start with the small ones.

answers.label: No, it's disrespect
answers.reply: It is. It tells others their time is worth less than yours.

answers.label: Depends on the cause
answers.reply: A sick child, fine. A long breakfast, no.

asks: When do you rise?
What hour do you get up? Exactly.

answers.label: Before dawn
answers.reply: Good. The best training is done in the dark.

answers.label: At dawn
answers.reply: Acceptable. Aim for an hour earlier.

answers.label: Late
answers.reply: Late. We'll fix that.

asks: And why that hour?
Your hour of rising. Habit, or choice?

answers.label: To train
answers.reply: The right answer.

answers.label: Habit
answers.reply: Habit is discipline that stopped complaining. Good.

answers.label: I like sleep
answers.reply: Hm. Honest. Sleep is training too. Up to a point.

asks: Is comfort the enemy of growth?
A warm bed, a full belly, an easy day. Good for a shinobi, or bad?

answers.label: Yes
answers.reply: Yes. Comfort is where strength goes to nap.

answers.label: No, rest matters
answers.reply: Rest matters. I'll concede it. Rest is not comfort, though.

answers.label: Too much of it is
answers.reply: Precisely. A little, earned. Never a lot, unearned.

asks: Why do you think people become shinobi? Not you, just people.
I've been reading about the first shinobi. What draws people to the life, do you think?

answers.label: To protect others
answers.reply: The oldest reason, and still the best, I suspect.

answers.label: For glory
answers.reply: Honest. The scrolls are full of people who wanted their names remembered.

answers.label: Their families expect it
answers.reply: Yes. Tradition carries as many as ambition does.

answers.label: Because they can
answers.reply: Ha. A talent wants using. There's something to that.

asks: And you? Of all the reasons people become shinobi, which is truly yours?
I've wondered since we talked. Why did you choose this path?

answers.label: To protect people
answers.reply: Then you chose well. Protecting is a reason that doesn't wear out.

answers.label: To matter to someone
answers.reply: That's honest, and rather brave to say. You matter here already.

answers.label: I'm not sure yet
answers.reply: A good answer. The ones who are sure early often change their minds.

asks: Is it always better to know the truth than not to know?
A scroll I read argued that ignorance can be a mercy. Do you agree?

answers.label: Always better to know
answers.reply: I lean that way too. A painful truth at least stands still.

answers.label: Not always
answers.reply: Hm. Some truths only wound. I can't say you're wrong.

answers.label: Depends who's asking
answers.reply: A careful answer. Truth needs a person ready to hold it.

asks: If you could keep only one scroll for the rest of your life, what kind would it be?
One scroll, forever. History, jutsu, stories, or something else?

answers.label: A history
answers.reply: Knowing where we came from. You'd never be bored.

answers.label: A book of jutsu
answers.reply: Practical. You'd be the most skilled hermit alive.

answers.label: A book of stories
answers.reply: A story you could read a hundred times. That's my choice too.

answers.label: A blank one, to fill
answers.reply: Oh, I like that. Your own scroll. Very wise.

asks: Which matters more, do you think: the past or the future?
Should we look back to learn, or forward to build?

answers.label: The past
answers.reply: The past is the teacher, the future only the exam. Well put, if I say so myself.

answers.label: The future
answers.reply: The future is where we'll actually live. Fair.

answers.label: Only today
answers.reply: Ha. The one day we're sure of. A philosopher's answer.

asks: If you could go back and change one choice you've made, would you? Or would that make you someone else?
Would you undo a mistake, if it meant losing what it taught you?

answers.label: I'd change it
answers.reply: Even at the cost of the lesson. Some mistakes aren't worth their tuition.

answers.label: No, it made me
answers.reply: Then you've made peace with it. That's rarer than wisdom.

answers.label: I'd have to think
answers.reply: The only truly honest answer, perhaps. Take your time.

asks: You find a mistake in a library scroll. A wrong date. Do you correct it, or tell the librarian?
A scroll at the library has an error in it. What's the proper thing to do?

answers.label: Tell the librarian
answers.reply: Correct, and courteous. The librarian will remember you fondly.

answers.label: Fix it myself
answers.reply: Bold! Scholars have duelled over less. Mind your brushwork.

answers.label: Leave a note inside
answers.reply: A note for the next reader. Gentle and clever.

asks: Do you think quiet people are underestimated?
The loudest voice in a room isn't always the wisest. Would you agree?

answers.label: Yes, often
answers.reply: I've found the same. Still water, as the saying goes.

answers.label: No, they choose it
answers.reply: Interesting. Quiet as a choice, not a lack. I'll think on that.

answers.label: Everyone is, somehow
answers.reply: Ha. True. We all see each other through a keyhole.

asks: What do you hope to understand by the time you're old?
If you could truly understand one thing in your life, what should it be?

answers.label: People
answers.reply: The hardest subject. No scroll covers it properly.

answers.label: Chakra
answers.reply: How it flows, why it works. The scroll keepers would hire you.

answers.label: Myself
answers.reply: The oldest question. Most of us run out of time on it.

answers.label: Everything
answers.reply: Ha! Then you'd best start reading tonight.

asks: And how will you go about understanding it?
Where would you even begin, learning something that big?

answers.label: Ask questions
answers.reply: The patient method. Ask, listen, ask again.

answers.label: Read everything
answers.reply: The library opens at eight. I'll introduce you to the good shelves.

answers.label: Live and watch
answers.reply: The slow way, and probably the truest.

asks: When you're feeling low, what food makes it better? I want to know for next time.
What do you eat when you need cheering up? Tell me, and I'll keep some by.

answers.label: Hot soup
answers.reply: Miso soup with tofu. I'll have a pot ready whenever you need it.

answers.label: Sweet buns
answers.reply: Red bean or custard? Both. I'll make both.

answers.label: Rice and pickles
answers.reply: Plain and honest. My grandmother swore by it.

answers.label: Anything someone made me
answers.reply: Oh, you. It's the making that counts, isn't it?

asks: That food you said cheers you up. Shall I make it for you one evening?
I've been practising your comfort food. May I cook it for you?

answers.label: Yes, please
answers.reply: Wonderful! Come hungry. I always make too much.

answers.label: Teach me to make it
answers.reply: Even better! A recipe lasts longer than a meal.

answers.label: Only if we eat together
answers.reply: Of course together. What else would I do, watch you eat?

asks: Have you eaten today? Properly, I mean. Not just a rice ball on the run.
When did you last have a proper meal? Be honest.

answers.label: Yes, a proper meal
answers.reply: Good. I can stop fussing. For a minute.

answers.label: Just a snack
answers.reply: A snack is not a meal. Sit. I'll find you something.

answers.label: I forgot
answers.reply: Forgot! Training all day on an empty stomach. Sit down this instant.

asks: Who looks after you when you're unwell?
When you catch a cold, who brings you tea?

answers.label: I manage on my own
answers.reply: On your own. Hm. I don't like the sound of that.

answers.label: My friends do
answers.reply: Good friends. Thank them for me.

answers.label: The hospital, if it's bad
answers.reply: The medics are wonderful. But a cold needs soup, not a ward.

answers.label: Nobody, really
answers.reply: Well. That changes now.

asks: Next time you're poorly, will you let me look in on you?
If you fall ill, promise you'll send word? I'll come with soup.

answers.label: Yes. Thank you
answers.reply: Good. That's settled. I feel better already.

answers.label: I'll be fine
answers.reply: You always say that. I'm coming anyway.

answers.label: Only if you bring soup
answers.reply: Ha! Soup is guaranteed. And a blanket. And another blanket.

asks: What makes a room feel cozy to you?
Picture the coziest room in the world. What's in it?

answers.label: A warm kotatsu
answers.reply: Legs under the blanket, an orange in hand. Perfect.

answers.label: People talking
answers.reply: Voices in the next room. That's the coziest sound.

answers.label: Something cooking
answers.reply: The smell of rice steaming. You're a person after my own heart.

answers.label: Piles of blankets
answers.reply: Ha! A blanket nest. I've got a few spare, you know.

asks: My neighbour's been alone since their old dog passed. How can I cheer them up?
There's someone on my street who's terribly lonely. What would you do?

answers.label: Visit every day
answers.reply: Every day, a little while. You're right. Showing up is half of it.

answers.label: Introduce a new puppy
answers.reply: The Inuzuka have a litter... it might be too soon. Or just right.

answers.label: Invite them to supper
answers.reply: A seat at my table. Of course. Why didn't I think of it?

answers.label: Ask what they need
answers.reply: Not guess. Ask. That's wise.

asks: My neighbour's smiling again! Should I keep visiting so often, or give them some room?
It worked. They're laughing on the porch again. Do I keep fussing?

answers.label: Keep visiting
answers.reply: Yes. Friendship isn't medicine you stop taking.

answers.label: Give them some room
answers.reply: You're right. Let them find their feet. I'll wave from the gate.

answers.label: Ask what they'd like
answers.reply: Ask again. You're always right about asking.

asks: When you're grown, will you have a house full of people, do you think?
Years from now, is your home a busy one or a quiet one?

answers.label: Full to the rafters
answers.reply: Noise and boots by the door and a big pot always on. Lovely.

answers.label: A few close ones
answers.reply: A small table with the right people. That's best of all.

answers.label: Peace and quiet
answers.reply: Quiet is good. Just leave the door open for me now and then.

asks: Should you keep being kind to someone who's never kind back?
There's a grump at the market I always greet, and they never greet back. Should I stop?

answers.label: Yes, always
answers.reply: That's what I think too. Kindness isn't a trade.

answers.label: Up to a point
answers.reply: Fair. Kindness shouldn't make you a doormat.

answers.label: No, it's wasted
answers.reply: Hm. Maybe. But I'll keep greeting them. Just in case.
